For the declared charge-$0$ node operators and a fixed residue $i$ and partition
$\lambda$, the orbit obtained by toggling the addable/removable $i$-cells of
$\lambda$ is a finite Boolean cube: the availability of one such cell is
unchanged by every other $i$-toggle, including $e=2$. Order the $i$-slots by
decreasing content, call a vertex state $+$ when the slot is occupied (addable)
and $-$ when it is empty (removable), so that the state word records the
configuration. Then the node operators on this cube are exactly the tensor
power $V(1)^{\otimes k}$ of the two-vertex rank-one string with the fixed
coproduct and $K$-exponent $q^{\#+-\#-}$; in particular the raw $A_0$-partition
span is stable under the actual normalized string operators, $f$ applies to the
first surviving $+$ and $e$ to the last surviving $-$ in decreasing-content
order, equivalently $f$ to the last $+$ and $e$ to the first $-$ in
increasing-content order, with $\varepsilon,\varphi$ the surviving minus/plus
counts. The standard partition form is the normalized rank-one polarization,
and all divided $E$- and $F$-powers have Laurent-integral matrices.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

With the declared use of the Axiom of Choice in the general integrable-module
decomposition, the empty connected component of the full partition crystal of
[[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]] is
the canonical highest weight crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$, with exactly the
$e$-regular labels. Its module is $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle$ and
its lower $A_0$-lattice is $M\cap F_0$; it occurs once. More precisely

$$F=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)},$$

a locally weight-finite indexed direct sum in which $p(k)$ is the number of
ordinary partitions of $k$; consequently
$\mathrm{ch}\,F=\mathrm{ch}\,V(\Lambda_0)\prod_{r\ge1}(1-e^{-r\delta})^{-1}$.
A highest **crystal** label need not be a highest **field** standard vector, and
the ambient canonical basis need not split these summands.

Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). We say that
$\lambda$ **dominates** $\mu$, and write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$, exactly when
$$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i\;\ge\;\sum_{i=1}^{r}\mu_i\qquad\text{for every }r\ge1,$$
where each sequence is padded with zeros beyond its number of parts; since both
partitions have total $n$, both sides equal $n$ for all $r$ at least the number
of parts of either, so the condition is a finite family of inequalities between
integers. We write $\lambda\rhd\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and
$\lambda\ne\mu$. The relation $\unrhd$ is the **dominance order** on the
partitions of $n$; we call $\lambda$ and $\mu$ **incomparable** when neither
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ nor $\mu\unrhd\lambda$ holds.

Because it is defined by a family of non-strict inequalities between integers,
$\unrhd$ is reflexive and transitive. It is also antisymmetric: if
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\mu\unrhd\lambda$, then the prefix sums of $\lambda$ and
of $\mu$ are equal for every $r\ge1$, and subtracting consecutive prefix sums
gives $\lambda_i=\mu_i$ for every $i$ (both sequences are eventually zero).
Hence $\unrhd$ is a partial order on the set of partitions of $n$. For $n\ge1$,
the partition $(n)$ is its unique maximum and the partition $(1^n)$ its unique
minimum: for every $\mu\vdash n$ and every $r\ge1$ one has
$$\min(r,n)=\sum_{i\le r}(1^n)_i\;\le\;\sum_{i\le r}\mu_i\;\le\;n=\sum_{i\le r}(n)_i .$$

For $n=0$ the order is the trivial order on the one-element set
$\{\varnothing\}$.

**Partitions.** Let $n\ge 0$ be an integer. A **partition of $n$** is a finite
weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ of positive
integers with $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_k=n$. Its entries are the **parts** of
$\lambda$ and $k$ is the **number of parts**. For $n=0$ the only partition is
the **empty partition** $\varnothing$, the empty sequence with $k=0$; for
$n\ge 1$ one has $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_k\ge 1$ and
$k\le n$. We write $\lambda\vdash n$. Trailing zeros are not parts: a finite
sequence of nonnegative integers ending in $0$ is not a partition, so the
number of parts of $\lambda$ is determined by $\lambda$ and
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ is a different data type from
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k,0)$.

**English Young diagrams.** The **(English) Young diagram** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$[\lambda]:=\{\,(i,j)\;:\;1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le \lambda_i\,\}\subseteq\mathbb N\times\mathbb N,$$
where $i$ numbers the **rows** downward and $j$ numbers the **columns**
rightward. An element of $[\lambda]$ is a **node**, or box, of the diagram. Row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ carries $\lambda_i$ nodes, and column $j$ carries
$$\lambda'_j:=\#\{\,i: \lambda_i\ge j\,\}$$
nodes, a quantity that is $0$ beyond the last column (and for every $j\ge1$ when $\lambda=\varnothing$). Since a partition is weakly
decreasing, $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$: if $[\mu]=[\lambda]$, then row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ is row $i$ of $[\mu]$, so $\mu_i=\lambda_i$ for every $i$
and $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $[\varnothing]=\emptyset$, the empty diagram.

**Conjugation.** The **conjugate partition** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$\lambda':=(\lambda'_1,\lambda'_2,\dots,\lambda'_{\lambda_1}),$$
the sequence of column heights of $[\lambda]$, with $\varnothing':=\varnothing$
for the empty partition. This is again a partition of $n$, and
$[\lambda']$ is the transpose of $[\lambda]$:
for $1\le i\le\lambda_1$ and $1\le j\le k$,
$$(i,j)\in[\lambda']\iff j\le\lambda'_i\iff \lambda_j\ge i\iff (j,i)\in[\lambda].$$
Outside these bounds neither diagram contains the corresponding node; for the empty partition both diagrams are empty.
Conjugation is an involution, $\lambda''=\lambda$, because
$\lambda''_i=\#\{j:\lambda'_j\ge i\}$ counts the columns of $[\lambda]$ of
height at least $i$, that is, the columns $j$ with at least $i$ rows of length
$\ge j$, which by weak decrease is exactly the set of $j\le\lambda_i$. Thus
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is a bijection on the partitions of $n$, exchanging
the number of parts with the largest part for nonempty partitions.

**Size zero.** The symmetric group of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is
$S_n:=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ ([[def-symmetric-group]]) for every
$n\ge 0$, and we fix
$$S_0:=\operatorname{Sym}(\emptyset)=\{1\},$$
the trivial group; for $n=0$ the set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is empty and the group
acts trivially on every size-zero object below. This is the convention used
whenever the constructions of this page are read at $n=0$.

A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: The normalized finite reversal bar. For a length-$r$ tuple $I$, put $t(I)$ equal to its number of unequal-residue pairs and define $\psi_r(u_I)=(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}q^{t(I)}u_{\operatorname{reverse}I}$, extended by $q\mapsto q^{-1}$. This descends through the finite straightening relations: an equal-residue swap relation reverses to itself, whereas every distinct-residue two-factor relation reverses, after coefficient bar, to $q$ times that relation. For the recursive relation its four terms are $u_l\wedge u_m+q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l+u_{m-b}\wedge u_{l+b}+q^{-1}u_{l+b}\wedge u_{m-b}$; reversal and coefficient bar give precisely $q$ times these same four terms. All terms preserve the residue multiset, so the global factor $q^{t(I)}$ is identical on the terms of a relation in a longer word. Thus the relation ideal is preserved. Applying reversal twice cancels the barred scalar and gives $\psi_r^2=1$. For the finite action the residue-count difference under a lowering move is $t(I^+)-t(I)=n_i-n_{i+1}-1$, and under its raising reverse it is $-(n_i-n_{i+1})-1$; substituting these identities into the fixed prefix coproduct converts its coefficient bar to the reversed suffix coproduct. Hence $\psi_r$ intertwines the generator bar, and its toral compatibility follows from weight preservation. These are finite computations in the relations of [F1].

Integral dominance triangularity. Straighten the reversed tuple of a normal wedge. The leading swap scalars cancel $(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}q^{t(I)}$, leaving the original wedge with coefficient $1$. Every other branch replaces an unequal pair by strictly more balanced interior indices with the same sum and residues. The sorted prefix sums therefore strictly decrease, so the corresponding partition is strictly dominated by the original one. All coefficients are Laurent integral and residues are preserved. Consequently on a finite degree the matrix of $\psi$ is dominance-unitriangular over $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. This conclusion is obtained from the finite relations, rather than assumed for the bar-correction equations.

Prefix independence and the charts. Let $m$ exceed the partition size and move a new minimum $u_{-m}$ through the prefix. Every secondary correction removes that minimum and leaves $m+1$ indices above $-m$ with total sum bounded by the ground sum plus size minus $m$, which is smaller than the minimum possible sum of $m+1$ distinct integers above $-m$; hence all secondary branches vanish because no normal tuple with that preserved sum exists by [F2], only the leading factor $(-1)^mq^{-\#\text{unequal}}$ survives, and it cancels the new normalization. Therefore $\psi$ and the corrections are prefix-independent, giving the actual infinity chart and the balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection; $F_A,F_0$ and the integral chart are kept separate.

The positive-$q$ correction. Proceed down a finite dominance refinement and suppose the already constructed lower vectors $G(\mu)$ are bar-fixed. The residual in $\psi(|\lambda\rangle)-|\lambda\rangle$, after prior corrections, is $\sum_\mu r_\mu(q)G(\mu)$. Since $\psi^2=1$, each coefficient satisfies $r_\mu+\overline{r_\mu}=0$. Writing a finite antisymmetric Laurent polynomial as $r=\sum_{k>0}a_k(q^k-q^{-k})$ gives the unique $c=\sum_{k>0}a_kq^k\in q\mathbb Z[q]$ with $c-\bar c=r$. Adding $cG(\mu)$ therefore kills that residual. Induction constructs the unique bar-fixed $G(\lambda)$ with leading standard vector and remainder in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ on strictly dominated shapes. All corrections remain in the original residue multiset, so their packed abacus runners, and hence their $e$-core, are unchanged. At each degree the triangular correction matrix and its inverse are integral polynomial matrices.

The basic lower basis. On $M$ the $A$-lattice of divided node actions maps into the partition $A$-lattice because the cube matrices are Laurent-integral; its lower lattice maps into $F_0$, and the lower global basis of [F3] is bar-fixed with regular crystal residues. By the balanced-triple uniqueness of [F3] the images agree with the unique ambient $G$'s of the regular degree, so every $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ lies in $M$ and the regular family is the lower global basis of $M$; no integral splitting or saturation is assumed, and the ambient basis is not claimed component-compatible.

The false transpose symmetry. The equality $d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ fails at $e=2$ and degree $4$: the recursion gives $d_{(2,1,1),(4)}=q$ while $d_{(1,1,1,1),(3,1)}=0$, since $(2,1,1)'=(3,1)$ and $4'=(1,1,1,1)$; the source symmetry statement concerns the bar transition matrix, not the lower matrix $D$. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use $(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients need the restricted Gram inverse, which may have rational entries.

Conclusion. The explicit wedge bar is involutive, prefix-independent and integral; the global basis $G(\lambda)$ is dominance-unitriangular with $q\mathbb Z[q]$ off-diagonal coefficients and same-core support, the $A$-and $A_0$-bases and the balanced intersection are as displayed, exactly the regular family is the lower global basis of $M=V(\Lambda_0)$, and the naive transpose symmetry of $D$ is false while the correct inverse/Gram rules hold.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is the first row of both tables: step 1.1 evaluates its single addable node of residue zero and its empty removable set, giving the exponent vector with a one in the first slot and zero raising action.

Zero entries are part of the layout: omitted terms have coefficient zero by the stated convention, and step 2.1's exponent column is computed so that individual entries are allowed to vanish or be negative, as in the middle entry at the two-cell partition.

The size-one partition is computed explicitly in both tables: step 1.1 gives its raising and lowering data at rank two with two addable nodes of the second color, and step 1.2 repeats the computation at rank three.

The rank-two double-edge table is the degenerate case and is computed separately: step 1.1 works it row by row with the two residues alternating along the boundary, so no entry is copied from the odd-rank table.

Both boundary ends of each node set are used: the signed counts are read from the smallest and from the largest content corners, as in step 1.1's evaluation of the two addable second-color nodes of the one-cell partition at contents one and minus one.

Every entry is a finite evaluation of explicit formulas on a finite list of partitions, and the tables themselves record the inputs, so nothing is selected. The Example's finite tables record every input of every evaluation.

boundaries.reason: The item is a finite table of evaluations asserting equalities of vectors and exponent lists; it contains no biconditional, so no forward implication is owed.
No converse claim is made: the source calibration is matched numerically rather than used to assert an equivalence, so there is no reverse direction to check.

citations.quote:
For a fixed residue $i$ list the addable and removable $i$-nodes of a partition
**by increasing content** $c-r$; larger content is read as further right or
higher. For an addable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\lambda$ (so that
$\mu=\lambda+\gamma$) define

$$N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\},$$

and for a removable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\mu$ (so that
$\lambda=\mu-\gamma$) define $N_i^l(\lambda,\mu)$ by the same formula inside the
smaller diagram $\lambda=\mu-\gamma$ with $>$ replaced by $<$, always excluding
$\gamma$ itself. The node formulas are then

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma)}|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{-N_i^l(\mu-\gamma,\mu)}|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

over the addable respectively removable $i$-nodes. The **node order** is the
content order just fixed, and it is used to define the finite signature
selection: a Chevalley coefficient minimiser is not in general a Kashiwara
arrow, and even a nonzero single Chevalley term can have zero crystal arrow.

Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and
$K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$.

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual
module structure, so nothing about $F$ is silently assumed in this Definition.

For every partition $\lambda$, every residue $i\in I$, and
$N_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}
-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\}$ one has

$$N_i(\lambda)=\delta_{i0}-\sum_{j\in I}a_{ij}\,m_j(\lambda),$$

where $m_j(\lambda)$ is the number of residue-$j$ cells of $\lambda$ and
$A=(a_{ij})$ is the cyclic affine type $A$ Cartan matrix. Consequently
$\sum_{i\in I}N_i(\lambda)=1$; the toral operator acts by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle=q^{\langle
h_i,\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)\rangle}$, the central product
$K_0K_1\cdots K_{e-1}$ acts by $q$, and $\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle)
=\Lambda_0-\sum_jm_j\alpha_j$ has level $1$. In particular
$N_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i0}$, and adding a node of residue $k$ changes $N_i$
by $-a_{ik}$, hence the weight by $-\alpha_k$.

Fix a residue $i$ and a partition $\lambda$, and write the **signature** of
$\lambda$ at $i$ as the word in the symbols $+$ (addable $i$-node) and $-$
(removable $i$-node) whose letters are the addable and removable $i$-nodes of
$\lambda$ read in the fixed increasing-content order of
[[def-the-node-order-and-n-i-exponents-for-fock-space]]. Reduce the word by
cancelling adjacent pairs $-+$ as long as such a pair remains. The surviving
minus letters are called **normal removable** $i$-nodes, and the first surviving
minus is the **good node** of $\lambda$ for $e_i$; the surviving plus letters
are called **conormal addable** $i$-nodes, and the last surviving plus is the
**cogood node** for $f_i$. If no sign of the required type survives, the
corresponding operator is $0$ on $|\lambda\rangle$. Equivalently, reading the
signature in decreasing content with the reversed symbols, one cancels $+-$
and takes the good node as the last surviving $-$ and the cogood node as the
first surviving $+$.

With the declared use of the Axiom of Choice in the general integrable-module
decomposition, the empty connected component of the full partition crystal of
[[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]] is
the canonical highest weight crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$, with exactly the
$e$-regular labels. Its module is $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle$ and
its lower $A_0$-lattice is $M\cap F_0$; it occurs once. More precisely

$$F=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)},$$

a locally weight-finite indexed direct sum in which $p(k)$ is the number of
ordinary partitions of $k$; consequently
$\mathrm{ch}\,F=\mathrm{ch}\,V(\Lambda_0)\prod_{r\ge1}(1-e^{-r\delta})^{-1}$.
A highest **crystal** label need not be a highest **field** standard vector, and
the ambient canonical basis need not split these summands.

The whole level-one Fock module has the crystal basis $(F_0,B_F)$ with
$F_0=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]|\lambda\rangle$ and
$B_F=\{|\lambda\rangle+qF_0:\lambda\text{ a partition}\}$. The normalized
Kashiwara operators remove the good normal $i$-node and add the cogood conormal
$i$-node of the corrected signature of
[[def-good-and-cogood-nodes-by-residue-signature-reduction]], and
$\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ are the surviving minus/plus counts. The graph is a
graph on all partitions, not only regular ones; its empty connected component
is precisely the set of $e$-regular partitions, while the $e$-restricted labels
belong to the transposed model. A pole or a unique Chevalley term does not
determine a crystal arrow.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

At $1$ the color-$1$ and color-$2$ additions give $2$ and $11$. This reproduces exactly the displayed arrows, and the raising arrows are their inverses.

Completeness and the boundary $111$. The shapes reached are exactly the $3$-regular shapes of size $\le3$; every other partition of size $\le3$, namely $111$, is not $3$-regular and lies outside the empty component by [F2]. At $111$ and color $0$ the signature has one top plus and one bottom minus which cancel, and the other colors have no surviving minus, so $111$ is a highest crystal vertex; its node residues are $0,2,1$, so its weight is $\Lambda_0-\alpha_0-\alpha_1-\alpha_2=\Lambda_0-\delta$. The statement that $111$ is highest as a crystal vertex is not the statement $E_i|111\rangle=0$ for the ordinary field operators.

Conclusion. The displayed graph is the empty component through size $3$, the shapes are the $3$-regular ones, and $111$ is the first highest crystal vertex outside it with weight $\Lambda_0-\delta$, with all weights computed from the node residues.

the lower global basis of $M$, identified by the two lower-global-basis
suppliers. The ambient basis is not automatically compatible with the other
field irreducible summands. The transpose equality
$d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ is **false** in general; the source symmetry

$(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients require the restricted Gram
inverse and need not be Laurent polynomials.

**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

(i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.

(ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.

(iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set $J$ need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual

derivations.claim: Strictness. By [F1] the full field decomposition contains the summands $V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)$ for every $k\ge0$ with multiplicity $p(k)\ge1$, and the $\Lambda_0$ summand occurs with multiplicity $p(0)=1$; since $p(k)\ge1$ for $k\ge1$ and those constituents are nonzero, $F$ is strictly larger than its $\Lambda_0$ constituent $M$.

Raw-vector exclusion. The shape $1^e$ is not $e$-regular: all its parts equal $1$ and occur $e$ times, so it lies outside the empty component by [F1]; since the residue basis of $F_0\cap M$ is exactly the empty component by [F3], every vector in $F_0\cap M$ has residue a combination of regular labels. The raw vector $|1^e\rangle$ has nonzero residue in $F_0/qF_0$ equal to the nonregular shape $1^e$, so $|1^e\rangle\notin M$; the same argument applies to $G(1^e)$, which is congruent to the same shape modulo $qF_0$.

The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation: it has strictly more constituents than the single $V(\Lambda_0)$, and even the explicit raw and lower-lift vectors $|1^e\rangle$ and $G(1^e)$ lie outside $M$; the nonregular ambient lower vectors are not a basis of a single highest module.

with diagonal $1$ and same $e$-core support; the family $\{G(\lambda)\}$ is an

and balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection. Exactly the $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ form

Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). We say that
$\lambda$ **dominates** $\mu$, and write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$, exactly when
$$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i\;\ge\;\sum_{i=1}^{r}\mu_i\qquad\text{for every }r\ge1,$$
where each sequence is padded with zeros beyond its number of parts; since both
partitions have total $n$, both sides equal $n$ for all $r$ at least the number
of parts of either, so the condition is a finite family of inequalities between
integers. We write $\lambda\rhd\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and
$\lambda\ne\mu$. The relation $\unrhd$ is the **dominance order** on the
partitions of $n$; we call $\lambda$ and $\mu$ **incomparable** when neither
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ nor $\mu\unrhd\lambda$ holds.

Because it is defined by a family of non-strict inequalities between integers,
$\unrhd$ is reflexive and transitive. It is also antisymmetric: if
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\mu\unrhd\lambda$, then the prefix sums of $\lambda$ and
of $\mu$ are equal for every $r\ge1$, and subtracting consecutive prefix sums
gives $\lambda_i=\mu_i$ for every $i$ (both sequences are eventually zero).
Hence $\unrhd$ is a partial order on the set of partitions of $n$. For $n\ge1$,
the partition $(n)$ is its unique maximum and the partition $(1^n)$ its unique
minimum: for every $\mu\vdash n$ and every $r\ge1$ one has
$$\min(r,n)=\sum_{i\le r}(1^n)_i\;\le\;\sum_{i\le r}\mu_i\;\le\;n=\sum_{i\le r}(n)_i .$$

For $n=0$ the order is the trivial order on the one-element set
$\{\varnothing\}$.

A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: The degrees $\le3$. Solving the triangular bar equations degree by degree with the reversal bar: in degree $2$ the only correction of $2$ is $q\,11$; in degree $3$ the partition $21$ is the only shape whose residue multiset forces no correction and $3$ receives the correction $q\,111$; the remaining shapes are bar-fixed. This gives the displayed degree-$\le3$ elements, and the basic labels are the $2$-regular ones, namely $\varnothing,1,2,3,21$, with $11$ and $111$ non-regular.

The degree-$4$ matrix. Repeating the finite bar recursion in degree $4$ gives the displayed five columns: the columns are $G(4)=|4\rangle+q|31\rangle+q|211\rangle+q^2|1111\rangle$, $G(31)=|31\rangle+q|22\rangle+q^2|211\rangle$, $G(22)=|22\rangle+q|211\rangle$, $G(211)=|211\rangle+q|1111\rangle$ and $G(1111)=|1111\rangle$, and the matrix is unitriangular with diagonal $1$; the basic columns are the regular labels $4$ and $31$. Every entry lies in $\mathbb Z[q]$ by [F1], and the dominance support is visible from the positions of the nonzero entries.

The false transpose symmetry. Conjugation of partitions sends $211\mapsto31$ and $4\mapsto1111$, so the transpose-conjugation equality would require $d_{(211),(4)}=d_{(1111),(31)}$; but the degree-$4$ matrix gives $d_{(211),(4)}=q$ and $d_{(1111),(31)}=0$. Hence the equality fails in general; the source's symmetry statement concerns the bar transition matrix $A$, not the lower matrix $D$.

Conclusion. The displayed elements are the actual lower global basis elements in degrees $\le4$, their coefficients are integral and dominance-triangular, the basic columns are the regular labels, and the naive transpose symmetry of $D$ is refuted by the explicit pair.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

A ring homomorphism whose kernel contains a two-sided ideal factors uniquely through the quotient ring.

If $I\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}R$, $f:R\to S$ is a ring homomorphism, and
$I\subseteq\ker f$, there is a unique ring homomorphism $\bar f:R/I\to S$ such
that $\bar f(r+I)=f(r)$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, steps
3.1 and 4.1).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: Finite rank-one orbits. Fix $i$ and $v\in V$. Then $W:=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv:a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace, where $A_i$ is the algebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$: the toral operator $K_i$ acts diagonally on the finitely many nonzero label components of $v$, so the vectors $K_i^cv$ range over a finite set; by [A3] there is $B$ with $E_i^bv=0$ for $b\ge B$; the mixed relation of [A2] rewrites any word in $E_i,F_i$ as a linear combination of words $F_i^aE_i^b$ with coefficients in the algebra generated by $K_i$; and for each $b<B$ and each of the finitely many $c$, local nilpotence of $F_i$ on the vector $E_i^bK_i^cv$ bounds the exponent $a$. The span of the resulting finite set is stable under $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$.

The second finite module. Fix $i\ne j$ and set $W':=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cF_jw:w\in W,\ a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$. Since $W$ is finite-dimensional, step 1.1 applied to each of the finitely many vectors $F_jw$ exhibits $W'$ as a finite union of finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspaces; hence $W'$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace of $V$ containing $F_jW$.

The rank-one adjoint module. On the finite-dimensional space $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ define operators by $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iTK_i^{-1}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. These are the values on generators of the standard adjoint action $a\cdot T=\sum a_{(1)}TS(a_{(2)})$ of the rank-one Hopf algebra $A_i$, for the coproduct $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, $\Delta(K_i)=K_i\otimes K_i$ and antipode $S(E_i)=-E_iK_i$, $S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i$, $S(K_i)=K_i^{-1}$. Since this is an action, the three operators satisfy the rank-one relations: $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^2\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$, $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^{-2}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ and $[\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)]=(\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)-\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Moreover $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$ is diagonalizable because $K_i$ acts diagonally on $W$ and $W'$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ are locally nilpotent: $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ raises and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ lowers the $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight by $2$, the weights of $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ form a finite set, and decomposing any $T$ into weight components each orbit is supported on distinct weights and hence terminates.

$F_j$ is a highest vector of weight $m$. Since $F_jW\subseteq W'$, the restriction $T:=F_j|_W$ lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$. By [A2], $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$ for $i\ne j$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i=0$; and by [A1], $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}T$, because $\langle\alpha_j,d_ih_i\rangle=d_ia_{ij}$. Put $m:=-a_{ij}\ge0$, the off-diagonal Cartan entries being nonpositive. Thus $T$ is annihilated by $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ and has $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight $q_i^m$ with $m\ge0$.

The rank-one string bound. Assume $T\ne0$. In the rank-one module $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ of steps 3.1-4.1 let $t\ge1$ be minimal with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$; it exists by the local nilpotence of step 3.1. For $b\ge1$ the divided-power formula of [F3] gives $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b)}(T)=\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}(T)$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $T$ by the scalar $\frac{1}{q_i^b-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{m-2s}-q_i^{-m+2s})=\frac{q_i^{m-b+1}-q_i^{-m+b-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}=[m-b+1]_i$, the two finite geometric sums evaluating to $\frac{q_i^b-q_i^{-b}}{q_i^{b-1}(q_i-q_i^{-1})}$ and $\frac{(q_i^b-q_i^{-b})q_i^{b+1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$. Taking $b=t$ and using $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$ together with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(t-1)}T=[t-1]_i!^{-1}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{t-1}T\ne0$ gives $[m-t+1]_i=0$, hence $m-t+1=0$ by [F2], that is $t=m+1$; therefore $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{m+1}T=0$.

The Serre sum. By induction on $n\ge0$, using $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=q_i^mT$ and the Pascal recurrence of [F4], the powers of the adjoint action expand as $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^n(T)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq_i^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$: the case $n=0$ is clear, and applying $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ to the formula for $n$, conjugating $K_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q_i^{m-2n}F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$ and comparing the coefficient of $F_i^{n+1-r}TF_i^r$ uses exactly $C_{n+1,r}=q_i^rC_{n,r}+q_i^{r-n-1}C_{n,r-1}$, the second form of [F4]. At $n=m+1=1-a_{ij}$ every Laurent exponent $r(m-n+1)$ is zero, so step 5.1 gives $\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ on $W$. Since every $v\in V$ lies in such a $W$ by step 1.1, the negative Serre relation holds as an operator on all of $V$.

The positive Serre relation. Put $E_i':=F_i$, $F_i':=E_i$ and $K_h':=K_{-h}$ for all $i$ and $h$. The primed data again satisfies the toral, toral-action, mixed and local-nilpotence hypotheses [A1]-[A3]: for instance $K_h'E_i'K_h'^{-1}=K_{-h}F_iK_h=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i'$, while $E_i'F_i'-F_i'E_i'=F_iE_i-E_iF_i=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_i'-K_i'^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Applying steps 1.1-6.1 to the primed data gives $\sum_{r}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r=0$ on $V$, which is the positive Serre relation for the original data.

Conclusion. By [A1]-[A3] the operators satisfy all the defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: the toral and toral-action relations, the mixed commutators, and both Serre families by steps 6.1 and 7.1. Hence the universal property [F1] equips $V$ with a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure; it is unique because $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by these operators, and it is a chosen $P$-graded type-one weight module by construction. derivations.claim: Coset decomposition of one appended strand. By the PBW basis [F1], every element of $R_{n+1}(Q)$ is a sum of monomials $\tau_wx^ae(\nu)$ with $w\in S_{n+1}$, and the right-coset decomposition $S_{n+1}=\bigsqcup_{a=1}^{n+1}S_ns_n\cdots s_a$ with additive lengths rewrites each such monomial, modulo the relations of [F2], in the form $\sum_a r_a\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ with $r_a\in R(n,1)=R(n)\otimes_kR(1)$; hence $R(n+1)=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n+1}R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ as $R(n,1)$-modules, and $R(n+1)$ is free of rank $n+1$ over $R(n,1)$.

Corners and the same-end structure. Multiply the decomposition of step 1.1 by the idempotents $e(n,i)$ on the left and $e(n,j)$ on the right. For $a\le n$ the term $e(n,i)\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ lies in the corner with first letter $i$ and last letter $i$; moving the idempotent past the crossings with [F2] shows that for $i\ne j$ the summands with $a>1$ vanish on the right idempotent $e(n,j)$ (the last strand carries the color $i$), while for $i=j$ the top summand $e(n,i)R(n,1)e(n,i)$ survives for every $a$. The explicit degree of $\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ on a fixed word is the sum of the crossing degrees $-b$ along the word, and the PBW leading terms show that $e(n,i)R(n+1)e(n,j)\cong q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_j)}\bigl(R(n)e(n-1,j)\otimes_{R(n-1)}e(n-1,i)R(n)\bigr)$ for $i\ne j$ and $e(n,i)R(n+1)e(n,i)\cong q^{-2d_i}\bigl(R(n)e(n-1,i)\otimes_{R(n-1)}e(n-1,i)R(n)\bigr)\oplus e(n,i)R(n,1)e(n,i)$ for $i=j$; the displayed shifts are exactly the source's $q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_j)}$ and $q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)}$.

The opposite-end exact sequence. By the same PBW-coset argument applied to the pair $(R(n),R_1(n))$ with $R_1(n)$ the image of the shift embedding $\xi_n$, the multiplication map $R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)$ is injective with image $\sum_{a=2}^{n+1}R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$, and the complementary coset $R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_1$ is free of rank one generated by $\tau_n\cdots\tau_1$ over $R(n,1)\cong R(n)\otimes k[x_{n+1}]$. The quotient map $\phi$ sends a PBW monomial to its coefficient on that coset, and the left multiplication by $x_{n+1}$ and the right multiplication by $x_1$ correspond under $\phi$ to multiplication by $t$ on $R(n)\otimes_kk[t]$; hence the displayed exact sequence of $(R(n),R(n))$-bimodules.

The mixed isomorphisms (a) and (b). Tensor the corner isomorphisms of step 2.1 with the formulation $E_iF_j(N)=e(\beta,i)R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,j)\otimes_{R(\beta)}N$ and $F_iE_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)\otimes_{R(\beta)}e(\beta,i)M$. For $i\ne j$ this yields $E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$; for $i=j$ the extra summand $e(n,i)R(n,1)e(n,i)\cong R(n)\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ of degree $2d_i$ survives and gives $E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$. The mirror computation with the left coset decomposition $S_{n+1}=\bigsqcup_a\tau_a\cdots\tau_1S(1,n)$ gives $\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$ for $i\ne j$ by the same vanishing of the nonidentity cosets.

The functorial sequence (c). Apply step 2.2 to $\beta+\alpha_i$ in place of $n$, restrict along $e(\beta,i)$ and tensor over $R(\beta)$ with $M$; since the first term of step 2.2 is exactly the kernel of the left-append induction and the quotient is $R(\beta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, the resulting sequence is $0\to\bar F_iE_iM\to E_i\bar F_iM\to q^{-(\alpha_i|\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\to0$, functorially in $M$, with the single q-shift coming from the difference of degrees between the two ends of the surviving coset, namely $-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$. Exactness of all functors is [F3].

Conclusion. Steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (a), (b) and (c) with their exact shifts in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; all identifications are corner-by-corner PBW computations, and no flatness of a quotient or unproved exactness of an induction is assumed beyond the freeness recorded in [F3].

derivations.claim: Monic splitting and the vertex ring. Over the universal coefficient ring $S=k[c_1,\dots,c_N]$, adjoin roots of the monic framing polynomial one at a time and divide by the root: at step $s$ the residual polynomial is monic of degree $N-s+1$, so ordinary monic division preserves monicity. This produces the Artin basis $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_N^{a_N}$, $0\le a_k\le N-k$, of the full root algebra; the pairing that reads the top coefficient has Gram matrix zero below the anti-diagonal and unit anti-diagonal in reversed order, hence is perfect over $S$, with no factorial division and no characteristic hypothesis. Block decomposition into the $r$ roots of $c_r$ and the $N-r$ roots of $b_{N-r}$ makes $L_m$ finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$, and $L_m=0$ for $r>N$ because then $p_m$ has degree below $r$.

The vertex ring as a matrix quotient. Representing $\mathrm{NH}_r$ as the matrix algebra on its Artin module (step 1.1, [F2]) shows that the two-sided ideal generated by a monic $p(X_1)$ is the matrix ideal of the coefficients of the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$, and monic division makes these coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive relations; hence $\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ is the matrix algebra over the monic factor ring $L_m$ of the Statement. The same computation shows the $i$-flag $B_m$ is free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, giving the two root extensions of the model.

The four coefficient maps and their triangles. For a monic $f$, the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is defined before imposing $f(X)=f(Y)=0$ and satisfies $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ and $\tau_XK_f=1$; therefore $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ for every $a$, which identifies $K_f$ with the dual-power-basis Casimir of the two monic coefficient forms. The two Casimirs of $b_{N-r}$ and $c_{r+1}$ give the four displayed cups and caps; their contractions are the identities $\sum_av_a\tau(z^ab)=b$ and $\sum_a\tau(bv_a)z^a=b$ for dual Artin bases, and substituting them into the tensor composites proves both triangles of each of the two adjunctions. Degrees: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$; the first maps have degree $0$ after the $B\{-2d_ir\}$ shift; the second cap has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_ir=-2d_i(h_m-1)$, with inverse degree on its unit. Restoring the normalized $H_i$ at its input weight produces exactly the four formal degrees of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]].

The rank-one intertwiner and its inverse. Splitting off one extra $i$-strand by the two-coset PBW decomposition [F3] gives the transfer term $\kappa_rb$ and the new-dot algebra as its complement; the rank-one intertwiner $g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2\kappa$ is verified to satisfy its quadratic and dot-commutation identities by expanding $\kappa X_{r+1}-X_r\kappa=1$ and $\kappa^2=0$. Multiplying these intertwiners along the extra strand and the other transfer by $p(X_1)$, then projecting to the polynomial complement, yields a coefficient map $A$ with $A(u^kS_r)=(-1)^ru^kp(u)$ where $S_r(u)=\prod_{a\le r}(u-X_a)^2$, and the same mixed relation gives $\phi_{k+1}(u)=u\phi_k+E(\psi_k)$; hence $A(u^k)=(-1)^r\operatorname{quo}_{S_r}(u^kp)$ by uniqueness of monic division, with no cyclotomic commutator theorem used as a supplier. If $h_m\ge0$ the quotients have distinct leading degrees $h_m+k$ and unit leading coefficients $(-1)^r$, so $\rho$ is the displayed (transfer, dot-power unit) map from $F_iE_i\{-2d_i\}$ plus the $h_m$ identity columns to $E_iF_i$, and its inverse subtracts the section and inverts the transfer. If $h_m\le0$ the map $A$ is surjective with kernel $\mathrm{span}\{1,u,\dots,u^{-h_m-1}\}$, and the connecting images have an anti-triangular dot/cap matrix with unit anti-diagonal, whose successive solution gives the negative-branch inverse. This verifies the rank-one matrix and both inverse equations of the formal definition.

Same-color crossing, curl and bubble identities. Equal crossings act by $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$, so $\kappa^2=0$, the braid relation holds and the two mixed dot equations follow from the rational divided-difference expansion; $K_f$ is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes and $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rank-one block inverse of step 4.1 produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: expanding $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the power bases and taking the top-coefficient rows gives the four signed sums over $a+b=-1$ and $a+b+c=-1$ with the stated orientation signs. The resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ of leading degree $h_m=N-2r$; its reciprocal is the opposite series with product $1$ coefficient by coefficient, forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings, since each existing $i$ root contributes one factor from each side of the cap. Appending an $i$ root $z$ changes $\Phi_i$ to $\Phi_i/(u-z)^2$ and appending a spectator $j$ root $y$ changes it to $\Phi_iQ_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$; expanding at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. At a monic vacuum, $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $h_\ell+\sum_jc_{\lambda_i-j}h_{\ell-j}=0$ with $h_0=1$, $h_{<0}=0$, so $H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$. All coefficients use only addition, multiplication and monic formal inversion.

Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient.

Mixed cups and caps with their constants. In $D[z]/p$ versus $D[z]/(pq)$ the coefficient form satisfies $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$, because $Q=t_{ij}q$ and the leading coefficient of $Qf$ is $t_{ij}$ times that of $f$. For a full existing $i$-string use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}\bigl(\Delta_r(X)X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_ap(X_a)\bigr)$, in which no $1/r!$ occurs; expanding parabolic divided differences verifies this over the universal integral coefficient ring, and over its generic-root fraction field the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant whose two factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator, so the identity is an integral polynomial identity and specializes to every field. With $p'=pq$ and $U_r=\prod_aQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA_{ij}}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$, and perfectness of the model forms makes $U_r$ injective on the old quotient. Testing the relative cap against these forms gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^{A_{ij}}t_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z)$ for every nil-Hecke coset element. Normalizing the second maps by the global weight sign $(-1)^{h+1}$ — legitimate because $N$ and $h$ have the same parity and the new $N$ changes by $A_{ij}$ — cancels that sign and gives the exact constant $t_{ij}$; dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation, and reversing colors gives $t_{ji}$ with the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist.

Conclusion. Steps 3.1-6.2 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers.
