Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

derivations.claim: Nil-Hecke branching. Put $z=t_r$ and write $E_a$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials in $t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}$. The relations $e_a=E_a+zE_{a-1}=0$ give $E_a=(-z)^a$ for $1\le a\le r-1$, and the top relation gives $z^r=0$; hence $C_r=k[t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}]\otimes_{k[E_1,\dots,E_{r-1}]}k[z]/(z^r)$ with $E_a$ acting by $(-z)^a$. The polynomial representation of $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ is free of rank $(r-1)!$ over its symmetric center and identifies $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ with the matrix algebra over that center; after the specialization its image on $C_r$ is $\mathrm{Mat}_{(r-1)!}(k[z]/(z^r))$ with standard column $C_r$. Therefore the graded socle and head of $C_r$ are each one shifted copy of the nil-Hecke simple, the simple composition coefficient is a shift of $[r]_i$, multiplication by $z$ has nilpotence index exactly $r$, the socle is the column over $z^{r-1}k$ and the head the column modulo $z$. For $r=1$ this reads $C_1=k$, $z=0$. The same computation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching, and matrix units plus a monic Artin basis make it valid in every characteristic.

Simple socle of one-step restriction. Let $S$ have $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ and let $U\subseteq E_iS$ be a simple subobject with $t=\epsilon_i(U)$. The final dot $z$ commutes with $R(\beta-\alpha_i)$ and acts nilpotently on $E_iS$ (positive dot degree and finite graded support), preserving the socle and its ungraded isotypic components; on the isotypic component containing $U$ a nonzero power of $z$ has a nonzero kernel copy of the same simple type killed by $z$, and absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let that copy be chosen homogeneously with the appropriate shift. Adjunction therefore produces a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L_1)\to S$, hence a surjection, and the shuffle bound [F4] gives $r\le t+1$ while the exact defining corners give $t\le r-1$; so $t=r-1$.

The maximal corner. Apply the maximal $(r-1)$-tail corner $p$ to $E_iS$, retaining $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)\otimes\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$. By [F3], $\Delta_i^rS\cong N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$, so $p(E_iS)=N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}}L(i^r)$; by step 1.1 and the absolute simplicity of $N$ this has a single simple socle. Every simple subobject $U$ of $E_iS$ has $t=r-1$ by step 1.2, so [F3] makes $pU$ a nonzero simple object; exactness of $p$ makes $p(\operatorname{soc}E_iS)$ semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of $p(E_iS)$. Hence $\operatorname{soc}E_iS$ is a single simple object, once, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; moreover every nonzero submodule of $E_iS$ contains a simple graded submodule whose $p$-image is nonzero (detection).

Simple head, detection and the dot index. Finite graded duality $D$ is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes corner idempotents and commutes with restriction, so applying step 2.1 to $DS$ (same $\epsilon_i$) and dualising gives a single simple head of $E_iS$, once; the nil-Hecke head and socle differ only by shift, so the two simple objects have the same shift orbit. On $p(E_iS)$, step 1.1 gives $z^r=0$ and $z^{r-1}\ne0$; the image of $z^r$ on all of $E_iS$ is a graded submodule with zero $p$-corner, so detection in step 2.1 forces it to be zero, while nonvanishing of $z^{r-1}$ in the corner forces it to be nonzero globally. Hence the last-dot nilpotence index on $E_iS$ is exactly $r$; repeating with the first variable gives first-dot index exactly $\epsilon_i^L(S)$.

Nonreduced induction and its unique head. Put $M_n=\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$, $n\ge1$. Its maximum tail is at most $r+n$ by the shuffle bound; at tail $r+n$ the Mackey filtration retains exactly all $n$ added $i$-strands together with $r$ terminal $i$-strands of $S$, so $\Delta_i^{r+n}M_n\cong N\boxtimes L(i^{r+n})$ up to the fixed shift — one actual surviving simple filtration term. Every simple quotient $T$ of $M_n$ has that maximum tail: adjunction gives a nonzero injection $S\boxtimes L(i^n)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^nT$, and restricting the first factor to the maximal $r$-tail retains a nonzero corner of $T$'s maximal corner, so $\epsilon_i(T)\ge r+n$, and the shuffle bound gives equality. Hence the finite semisimple head of $M_n$ has only constituents detected by its simple maximal corner, so it is one simple constituent, once; the kernel of $M_n\to\operatorname{hd}M_n$ has zero maximal corner, so every other composition factor has smaller $\epsilon_i$ and the head occurs exactly once in the whole composition series. Write $f_iS:=\operatorname{hd}M_1$.

Partial inverses, iterates and the cyclotomic criterion. Adjunction realises $S$ in $E_i(f_iS)$, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{soc}E_if_iS=S$ with shifts restored; conversely $S=\operatorname{soc}E_iT$ implies $T$ is a simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L_1)$, hence $T=f_iS$. Thus one-step socle and head are partial inverses, $f_i$ raises $\epsilon_i$ by one and $\operatorname{soc}E_i$ lowers it by one; iterating the one-strand argument gives $\operatorname{hd}\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))=f_i^nS$. Let $J^\Lambda$ be generated by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ on every word beginning with $i$; it annihilates a simple $S$ exactly when each first-$i$ corner has first-dot index at most $\lambda_i$, which by step 3.1 is $\epsilon_i^L(S)$, so $J^\Lambda S=0$ iff $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$; if a generator is nonzero, simplicity forces $J^\Lambda S=S$. Right restriction preserves first strands, hence the cyclotomic subcategory; for induction, the generic unique head either survives, in which case the quotient induction has the same head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero because every nonzero finite module has a simple quotient. The maximal-$\epsilon$ composition part is the same simple shift orbit as the head and socle, with coefficient a shift of $[r]_i$ by step 1.1. No choice and no self-dual representative is used.

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag

formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero

$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color

degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

derivations.claim: Bubble slides on the model. For an $i$ root $x$ the normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$, and for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$ with $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ of constant coefficient $1$. These hold directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator root multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$; every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These are the specified formal relations, checked on the model and not derived from the faithfulness being proved.

Straightening to normal form. Move dots to fixed component positions using cyclicity and the KLR dot moves; an equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap towards a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations: a main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles, and a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite because open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at each fixed total degree; adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair (unsorted extrema, remaining crossing obstacles) and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion plus the KLR braid and quadratic straightening then reduce every open matching to the selected reduced diagram, all braid defects being shorter. This gives a finite spanning family of reduced matchings with dot monomials and far-left bubble monomials.

All-downward boundaries. At an all-downward boundary every open arc joins bottom to top, so it is a colored permutation; the reduced matching together with its dots is exactly a KLR PBW monomial, and the morphism space is the PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in the positive bubble family, whose opposite family is the coefficientwise reciprocal by bubble inversion. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$-endpoints to the other boundary, and the straightening of step 2.1 has unit leading matching coefficients, so the same normal form transfers.

Independence by degree separation. Fix the physical source weight $\mu$ and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$; choose spectator background counts $m_j$ with $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$ and for an increasing background $i$-count $r$ set $N=\mu_i+2r$, $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$, so the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ is fixed. Use the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_ia$, put $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod_a(u-x_a)$; the normalized series $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U(t)$ with $U_0=1$ has coefficients $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$, unit triangular in the framing variables, with reciprocal coefficients $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Hence the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, in every characteristic and at every physical weight; no unit old-root coefficient is claimed, since $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two. A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after this triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain; the generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word, so a polynomial test vector with nonzero output exists after clearing a finite denominator. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and $B$ the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output, both finite in the untruncated polynomial ring, and let $L$ bound the number of added $i$-flags tested. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$, spectator appends only increase $N$, all variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive; choosing $r\ge0$ and $\lambda_i\ge D$ with $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$ (possible at fixed $\mu$) separates all model relations from degree $\le B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model.

Conclusion. The family of step 2.1 spans every morphism space by a finite straightening, and step 4.1 shows that no nonzero combination of its reduced matchings, dot monomials and independent bubble monomials vanishes in some graded flag model, so the family is a basis and the stated models are jointly faithful. The model's ordered word shifts with $i$ last make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$, and the formal upward generator is the normalized $H_i$, so the witness is a witness in the specified graded model; the assertion concerns the formal proof category before any cyclotomic quotient transfer.

annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

derivations.claim: The comparison maps. By the PBW basis [F1] the right $A[t]$-modules $K_0=Se_R/Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e_R$ and $K_1=Se_L/Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e_L$ are finite projectives, where $t$ records the appended dot. With the source substitution $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$, define $P(u)=ua(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ and $Q(v)=vg_n\cdots g_1$, where $g=\kappa$ at unequal colours and $g=(y-x)-(y-x)^2\kappa$ at equal colours. Moving each dot and crossing across the appended strand shows block bilinearity, and expanding the cyclotomic ideal along the left cosets shows $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0\to R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e_R)$.

Monic annihilators and projectivity, locally. Let $0\to P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0\to M\to0$ be an exact sequence of right $A[t]$-modules with finite projective $P_0,P_1$, and suppose a central monic $f$ annihilates $M$. Multiplication by $f$ is injective on a free $A[t]$-module by its unit leading coefficient, hence on its projective summands. On a finite free module monic division gives an $A$-linear operator $p_{\mathrm{free}}$ taking a polynomial to its quotient by $f$, with $p_{\mathrm{free}}(xf)=x$. Choose split inclusion $u:P_1\to A[t]^N$ and projection $v:A[t]^N\to P_1$; then $p=vp_{\mathrm{free}}u$ satisfies $p(xf)=x$ on $P_1$, since $u$ is $A[t]$-linear and $vu=1$. Since $fM=0$, multiplication by $f$ on $P_0$ has image in $j(P_1)$, defining $h:P_0\to P_1$ by $jh=f$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $hj=f$ on $P_1$, so $phj=1$. Thus $j$ has the $A$-linear retraction $ph$, and $M$ is a direct summand of the $A$-projective module $P_0$ and is $A$-projective. Equivalently, $P_r/fP_r$ is a summand of $(A[t]/fA[t])^N\cong A^{mN}$ and is $A$-projective, which is the monic-quotient reason for the splitting. This argument uses finite projective presentations and division and does not assume $f$ invertible or the target $M$ projective.

The monic comparison and its quotient. The local quadratic and braid calculation gives $QP=a_i(t)\prod_{
u_a
e i}Q_{i
u_a}(t,x_a)$ on each word corner of $K_1$, with a uniform unit leading coefficient. This is a polynomial endomorphism of the finite projective $A[t]$-module $K_1$; the injectivity argument of step 1.2 applies, so $QP$ and therefore $P$ are injective. Together with the image-kernel computation of step 1.1, this gives the actual projective resolution $0	o q^sK_1\xrightarrow{P}K_0	o Be_R	o0$, where $B=R^\Lambda( eta+\alpha_i)$ and $s=(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda- eta)$. The target is the cokernel $Be_R$, whereas $K_0,K_1$ are the projective comparison modules over $A[t]$. No cyclicity of $K_0$ or $K_1$ follows or is required.

Projectivity of the cyclotomic bimodules. The appended dot on $M=Be_R$ is annihilated by a central monic scalar-coefficient polynomial by [F2]. Apply step 1.2 to the projective $A[t]$-resolution in step 2.1, with $M=Be_R$, to conclude that $Be_R$ is right $A$-projective. This module is finitely generated over $A$: its finite $A[t]$-generators together with dot powers below the degree of the annihilator generate it over $A$. In the homogeneous standard case the resolution and $M$ are graded; decompose the resulting $A$-linear splitting into homogeneous components on finite homogeneous generators, and take its degree-zero component to get a graded splitting. The generator-fixing anti-involution sends $Be_R$ to $e_RB$ and converts this right projectivity into left $A$-projectivity. The same monic argument is valid for arbitrary ungraded monic cyclotomic deformations.

Exactness and preservation. Tensoring by the right $A$-projective module $Be_R$ is exact, so $F_i^\Lambda$ is exact, and idempotent restriction $E_i^\Lambda$ is exact. The left $B$-module $Be_R$ is a direct summand of $B$, hence induction sends any projective $A$-module, presented as a summand of a free module, to a projective $B$-module; finite generators remain finite under induction. A finitely generated projective $B$-module is a summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of $B$, and its restriction is consequently a summand of the corresponding finite direct sum of shifts of $e_RB$. Left $A$-projectivity and finite generation of $e_RB$ from step 3.1 therefore show that restriction preserves finitely generated projectives. These arguments apply ungraded to monic deformations as well.

The exact sequence (c). Tensor the bimodule resolution $0\to q^sK_1\xrightarrow{P}K_0\to Be_R\to0$ of step 2.1 over $A$ with a left $A$-module $M$. It remains exact because its cokernel $Be_R$ is right $A$-projective by step 3.1, so the original sequence is split as a sequence of right $A$-modules. By their definitions in step 1.1, $K_1\otimes_A M$ is the left-append generic induction $\bar F_iM$ and $K_0\otimes_A M$ is the right-append generic induction $F_iM$, while $Be_R\otimes_A M=F_i^\Lambda M$. The map $P$ is left $R(\beta+\alpha_i)$-linear and has homogeneous degree $s=(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)$, giving exactly the functorial sequence in (c) in the declared target category. On the ungraded monic-deformation branch the same sequence is interpreted without a grading shift.

Conclusion. Steps 3.1-4.2 prove (a), (b) and (c) with the displayed shift, in the graded standard case with graded projectives and verbatim ungraded for a monic deformation; the comparison is monic and no filtered-colon citation is used.

citations.quote:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced
perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and
monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form
a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of
weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW
corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the
opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial
flag models of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each
fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this
formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

derivations.claim: Vacuum coefficients are forced. Use the normalized trace cups and caps of [F1] and let $h_\ell$ be the bubble closed with $\lambda_i-1+\ell$ dots, with negative-dot symbols extended by the formal inversion of [F1]. The rank-one identities give $h_\ell=0$ for $\ell<0$ and $h_0=1$. Closing $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ for $\ell\ge1$ is lawful in the defining ideal because the exponent $\ell-1$ is nonnegative even when some resulting bubble indices are negative, and gives $h_\ell+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{\ell-\lambda_i}=0$. Hence $H(t)=\sum_{\ell\ge0}h_\ell t^\ell$ is the inverse of $a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$, and bubble inversion gives $A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)$; each coefficient uses only a finite recurrence. An actual vacancy loop with $r\ge0$ dots has $A$-index $\lambda_i+1+r$ and vanishes because $A$ has degree at most $\lambda_i$, while the $A$-coefficients of index $1,\dots,\lambda_i$ are fake bubbles of negative dot count, prescribed rather than zero; for $a_i=u(u-1)$ one gets $A=1-t$, $H=(1-t)^{-1}$, so setting all positive bubbles to zero would wrongly change the deformation. If $\lambda_i=0$ then $a_i=1$ kills $F_iv$ and $A=H=1$.

Every bubble coefficient is brought to the vacuum. After bending, a coefficient may be a bubble at $\Lambda+\alpha_i$ immediately to the left of an added first $i$-strand with dot $z$; the rank-one bubble-slide equation in coefficient normalization is $A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda(t)$ and $H_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^{-2}H_\Lambda(t)$. These are normalized power series with constant coefficient $1$, and for each fixed coefficient the equation is finite polynomial in $z$ and the vacuum coefficients; negative exponents of $(1-zt)$ denote formal coefficient recursion. The algebraic verification is the model computation: with total monic polynomial $p$ and existing-root factor $c_r$ the normalized series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, and adding the distinguished root $z$ replaces $c_r^{\mathrm{rev}}$ by $c_r^{\mathrm{rev}}(1-zt)$ and leaves $p^{\mathrm{rev}}$ unchanged; passing to the reciprocals gives the displayed pair.

Specializing the vacuum coefficients adds no downward relation. Let $S$ be the vacuum bubble coefficient specialization of step 1.1. By the recurrence $S$ is contained in $J$. By the tensor-product normal form [F2], specializing these central vacuum coefficients alone gives the all-downward corner $R(\beta)$ with no relation imposed in its ordinary polynomial and crossing part; this uses the normal form, not a flatness assertion. One may therefore compute in $\mathcal P_i/S$ first and then include the $E_i$ and first-strand generators, with every bubble coefficient brought to the vacuum by step 2.1.

The corner identification. Let $x\in J\cap e(
u)R( eta)e(\mu)$. Expanding $x$ in the normal form of [F2] and using steps 2.1-3.1 to substitute every bubble coefficient by its vacuum value, $x$ is a combination of the generators $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ whiskered and composed with downward diagrams; the whiskering of $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ into a downward word contributes only the first-strand $a$-terms through the triangles, while the $a_j(x)$-generators contribute exactly the ordinary two-sided ideal $I_a( eta)=\sum_jR( eta)a_j(x_1)e(j, eta-\alpha_j)R( eta)$. Conversely every element of $e(
u)I_a( eta)e(\mu)$ lies in $J$ by construction. Hence the intersection is exactly $e(
u)I_a( eta)e(\mu)$, and the same expansion shows the map from the ordinary monic cyclotomic corner $e(
u)R( eta)e(\mu)/e(
u)I_a( eta)e(\mu)$ to the corresponding Hom corner of $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism compatible with composition.

Conclusion. Steps 1.1-4.1 prove the forced vacuum specialization, the corner equality and the isomorphism, over every degree-zero field and for the whole admissible homogeneous $Q$ family; in the inhomogeneous monic case the same argument is performed without grading and asserts only the ungraded corner equality, and no finite-type, characteristic-zero, faithfulness or generic Frobenius input is used.

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the comultiplication's $E_i,F_i$ formulas are
unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

derivations.claim: Finite reduction and two elementary tools. Restrict every containing-weight argument to the finite colour support of the modules and the finitely many selected strings by [F2]; all bounds and coordinates are then finite and the algebras, Cartan data and parameters are unchanged. For an exact induction functor: if $\operatorname{Ind}(A,H)\to T$ is surjective with $T$ simple, choose the first term of a composition series whose induced image is nonzero; that image is $T$ and the previous term maps to zero, giving a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ from some simple composition factor $U$. If $\epsilon_i(A)=0$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ is nonzero with $U,T$ simple, then $\epsilon_i(T)=\epsilon_i(U)$: the shuffle bound gives $\epsilon_i(T)\le\epsilon_i(U)$, and adjunction injects $A\otimes U$ into the restriction of $T$, whose terminal $\epsilon_i(U)$ corner is nonzero, giving the reverse inequality.

The jump lemma. Adjunction for $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L(j))\to f_jM$ together with the shuffle bound gives $c_i(M)\le c_i(f_jM)\le c_i(M)+\delta_{ij}$. For $i\ne j$ this is equality, and first-end symmetry gives $\epsilon_i(f_j^LM)=\epsilon_i(M)$. Suppose $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+1$: the reversed induction $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i),M)$ has the same ungraded character as $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L(i))$, hence the same ungraded composition factors, and its unique maximal-first-tail factor is $f_i^LM$ once, so $f_iM=f_i^LM$; conversely this equality forces the increase. Since finite duality commutes with $e_i,f_i$ on shift orbits, $\operatorname{coInd}(M,L_n)$ has simple socle $f_i^nM$, and the positive-shift coinduction formula gives $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_n)=(f_i^L)^nM$ and $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(L_n,M)=f_i^nM$ on shift orbits.

Increase persists; the jump index. If $f_iM=f_i^LM$ then the same simple is head and socle of $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$, occurring once in the whole composition series by [F1]; a finite-length module with a simple socle equal to its head occurring once is simple (otherwise the socle lies in the radical and gives a second occurrence of the head). Hence $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$ is simple and equals $\operatorname{Ind}(L_1,M)$, and iterating gives $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_n)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_n,M)$ up to shift, with simple unique head and socle for every $n$; in particular $c_i(f_i^nM)=c_i(M)+n$ for all $n$, so once $c_i$ increases it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Set $J_i(M)=\max\{n:c_i(f_i^nM)=c_i(M)\}$; the separate root-height induction with the two-colour growth and the annihilation lemma bounds it without presuming integrability in an unbounded $i$-direction, and once finite the zero-jump lemma gives $J_i(f_iM)=\max(0,J_i(M)-1)$. Combining with the one-step formula $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+[f_iM=f_i^LM]$ yields $J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for $\beta=\operatorname{wt}(S)$, the claimed formula.

Strict elementary embeddings. With $\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}\rangle$, the one-step socle/head identities make $\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ a strict injective elementary-crystal map: extraction increases by $c_i(S)$ on the image and the weight is shifted by $-c_i(S)\alpha_i$, and the assignment is injective on simple shift orbits by the uniqueness of the socle in [F1]. Every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at some colour, since otherwise each $\epsilon_i^L$ vanishes and the module would be a vacuum; the simple graph is lowering-generated because every generic $f_i$ is nonzero by [F1] and $e_i$ recovers the source on shift orbits.

citations.quote:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).

Let $R=\bigoplus_\beta R(\beta)$ be a KLR algebra on a symmetrizable Cartan datum
with no imaginary simple roots
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]) and let
$E_i$ denote restriction $e(\beta,i)(-)$ and $F_i$, $\bar F_i$ the right-append
and left-append inductions of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]
(so that $\bar F_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(i,\beta)\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$ with
$e(i,\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(i\ast\nu)$). Let $t_i$ be an indeterminate of
degree $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2d_i$. Then:

(a) for $i\ne j$ there are natural isomorphisms
$E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$ and
$\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$;

(b) for $i=j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$,
where $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])(M)=M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ homogeneous
of degree $2d_i$;

(c) the opposite-end corner comparison gives a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta))$
$$0\longrightarrow \bar F_iE_iM\longrightarrow E_i\bar F_iM\longrightarrow q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\otimes_kk[t_i]$ is understood in the graded sense. Equivalently, there
is an exact sequence of $(R(n),R(n))$-bimodules
$0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk[t]\to0$ in the
notation of the source, with the bimodule structures induced by the embeddings
$\xi_n$. All shifts are computed in the fixed grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; the functors are exact
([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

derivations.claim: Monic division and the positive branch. The recurrence in step 1.1 implies $\mathcal A(at)-\mathcal A(a)t\in A$ for every $a\in A[t]$. Induction on $m$ therefore gives $\deg_t(\mathcal A(af)-\mathcal A(a)f)<m$ whenever $f$ has degree $m$: for $f=tg$, write the difference as $\mathcal A(atg)-\mathcal A(at)g+(\mathcal A(at)-\mathcal A(a)t)g$, and use the degree-$m-1$ case on the first term. Applying this to the central monic $S$ and $a=t^k$, together with $\mathcal A(t^kS)=\gamma^{-1}t^kW$, gives $t^kW=(\gamma\phi_k)S+r_k$ with $\deg_t r_k<2p$. Thus ordinary monic division proves that $\gamma\phi_k$ is precisely the quotient of $t^kW$ by $S$; no $A[t]$-linearity of the snake map is assumed. For $h\ge0$ the quotients have distinct unit leading degrees $h+k$, so $\mathcal A$ is injective with polynomial remainder basis $1,t,\dots,t^{h-1}$; the dotted ordinary-unit columns split its cokernel. The positive snake sequence is $0\to q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\to E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\to\operatorname{coker}\mathcal A\to0$; the dotted ordinary-unit columns give a section of its last map, hence the natural isomorphism $q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ of part (a).

The negative branch. For $h=-r\le0$, the same division shows $\mathcal A$ is surjective with kernel spanned by $1,t,\dots,t^{r-1}$. The dotted multiplication-counit rows on that kernel are anti-triangular with unit source diagonal $\gamma^{-1}$ (equivalently native diagonal $-\gamma^{-1}$), so their finite recursive inverse splits the kernel; the snake sequence then gives $q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{r-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}$, which is part (b).

Bimodule form and conclusion. Evaluating the natural isomorphisms of steps 2.1 and 3.1 on the object $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ and using the internal shift convention of [F3] gives the displayed isomorphism of graded $A$-bimodules; For $i\ne j$ the generic mixed corner map also descends to the cyclotomic quotients. To see this directly, expand the first-strand cyclotomic ideal by the same PBW cosets: besides terms where its generator lies in the source or target rank-$n$ algebra, the only term has the generator fully transferred to the left endpoint and back. In the $(i,j)$ corner that term has the factor $e(i,\beta')a(x_1)e(j,\beta')=0$, since the two endpoint idempotents are orthogonal and commute with the first dot. Thus the corner ideal is exactly the sum of the source and target induced cyclotomic ideals. Quotienting the generic map by these two ideals gives $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}F_j^{\mathrm{basic}}\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_j^{\mathrm{basic}}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$. This endpoint argument concerns unequal colors; the equal-color relation is instead the split snake sequence already proved. Both branches are proved by division and finite recursion, and local nilpotence is not used to guess the summand count.
