Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, so that $l=p_n$ is the number
of columns, and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$
is in bijection with $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$ via
$(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$, and
$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$
and $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This
grading is the type-A pyramid good grading of the source, not the Dynkin
grading attached to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple.

All matrix spaces below carry the commutator bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$ and are
Lie subalgebras of $\mathfrak{gl}_m(\mathbb C)=M_m(\mathbb C)$ in the sense of
[[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]; closure under the bracket is verified in
each case by the computation displayed.

* The **general linear Lie algebra** $\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)=M_n(\mathbb C)$,
  for $n\ge1$. The **special linear Lie algebra**
  $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb C)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):\operatorname{tr}A=0\}$
  is a Lie subalgebra because $\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$, and
  $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ agrees with
  [[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]].
* The **symplectic Lie algebra** $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ is the set of
  $A\in M_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ with $AJ+JA^{T}=0$, for $n\ge1$, where
  $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\-I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$.
* The **orthogonal Lie algebras** $\mathfrak{so}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ and
  $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}(\mathbb C)$ are the sets of $A\in M_m(\mathbb C)$ with
  $AJ+JA^{T}=0$, for $n\ge1$, where $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$ for
  $m=2n$ and
  $J=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&I_n\\0&I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$ for $m=2n+1$.

Solving $AJ+JA^{T}=0$ blockwise gives
$A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&-a^{T}\end{pmatrix}$ for the symplectic and even
orthogonal cases, with $b,c$ symmetric for $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ and
$b,c$ skew-symmetric for $\mathfrak{so}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$, and gives
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&u&-w^{T}\\ w&a&b\\ -u^{T}&c&-a^{T}\end{pmatrix},\qquad u\in M_{1\times n}(\mathbb C),\quad w\in M_{n\times1}(\mathbb C),\quad b,c\ \text{skew-symmetric},$$
for $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}(\mathbb C)$. In particular
$\dim\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb C)=n(2n+1)=\dim\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}(\mathbb C)$
and $\dim\mathfrak{so}_{2n}(\mathbb C)=n(2n-1)$. Each set is closed under the
bracket: if $AJ=-JA^{T}$ and $BJ=-JB^{T}$, then
$[A,B]J+J[A,B]^{T}=ABJ-BAJ+JB^{T}A^{T}-JA^{T}B^{T}$, and substituting
$AJ=-JA^{T}$ and $BJ=-JB^{T}$ (equivalently $JA^{T}=-AJ$ and $JB^{T}=-BJ$) makes
the four terms cancel in pairs. For $n\ge1$, each symplectic or orthogonal family is a nonzero proper subspace of
$M_m(\mathbb C)$ closed under the commutator, hence a Lie subalgebra.

For a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ over $k$ and a $\mathfrak g$-module $M$,
the degree-$n$ **Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains** are

$$C^n(\mathfrak g,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Lambda^n\mathfrak g,M)\quad(n\geq0).$$

Set $C^n(\mathfrak g,M)=0$ for $n<0$. Since
$\Lambda^0\mathfrak g=k$, evaluation at $1$ identifies
$C^0(\mathfrak g,M)$ with $M$. Cochains may equivalently be viewed as
alternating $n$-linear maps $\mathfrak g^n\to M$. No finite-dimensionality
or characteristic hypothesis is needed. If $n>\dim\mathfrak g$ in the
finite-dimensional case, the exterior power and hence the cochain space are
zero.

For $f\in C^n(\mathfrak g,M)$ define $df\in C^{n+1}(\mathfrak g,M)$ by

$$\begin{aligned}(df)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)={}&\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i x_i f(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_n)\\&+\sum_{0\leq i<j\leq n}(-1)^{i+j}f([x_i,x_j],x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_n).\end{aligned}$$

This fixes a zero-based sign convention. A hat means omission, and in the
second sum the bracket is inserted as the first argument. Empty sums are
zero. Thus for $m\in C^0=M$, $(dm)(x)=xm$. Alternation of the formula makes
it factor through $\Lambda^{n+1}\mathfrak g$; the next theorem proves that
successive differentials compose to zero.

The **Lie algebra cohomology** of $\mathfrak g$ with coefficients in the
$\mathfrak g$-module $M$ is the cohomology of its Chevalley–Eilenberg
cochain complex:

$$H^n(\mathfrak g,M)=\frac{\ker(d:C^n\to C^{n+1})}{\operatorname{im}(d:C^{n-1}\to C^n)}.$$

The containment of the denominator in the numerator is supplied by
[[thm-the-chevalley-eilenberg-differential-squares-to-zero]]. For $n<0$ all
cochain groups, and hence all cohomology groups, are zero by convention. This
definition is valid without finite-dimensionality or a characteristic
restriction.
$$H^0(\mathfrak g,M)=M^{\mathfrak g}=\{m\in M:xm=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathfrak g\}.$$

For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$ and a short exact sequence
$0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ of $\mathfrak g$-modules, the induced CE
complexes form a degreewise short exact sequence and yield the natural long
exact sequence

$$\cdots\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M')\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M)\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M'')\to H^{n+1}(\mathfrak g,M')\to\cdots.$$

Keep the type-A pyramid data
$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], with
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism
with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a Lie algebra over $k$. In $T(\mathfrak g)$, regard
$[x,y]\in\mathfrak g$ as an element of tensor degree one, and let $I$ be the
two-sided ideal generated by

$$x\otimes y-y\otimes x-[x,y]\qquad(x,y\in\mathfrak g).$$

The **universal enveloping algebra** is

$$U(\mathfrak g)=T(\mathfrak g)/I.$$

Write

$$\iota_{\mathfrak g}:\mathfrak g\longrightarrow U(\mathfrak g)$$

for the composite of the degree-one inclusion with the quotient map. This
definition makes $U(\mathfrak g)$ a unital associative algebra and $\iota_{\mathfrak g}$ a
linear map. It does not assert that $\iota_{\mathfrak g}$ is injective; that conclusion will
come from PBW.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring ([[def-commutative-ring]]) and let $I$ be a set.
The set $R[x_i:i\in I]$ consists of the functions

$$c:\mathcal M(I)\longrightarrow R$$

with finite support, where $\mathcal M(I)$ is the monoid of
[[def-monomials-on-an-index-set]]. We write such a function as the formal sum
$\sum_a c_a x^a$. Addition is pointwise. Multiplication is the convolution

$$(cd)_u:=\sum_{a+b=u}c_a d_b,$$

where only pairs in $\operatorname{supp}(c)\times\operatorname{supp}(d)$
contribute and the sum is the finite sum of
[[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]. The constant $r\in R$ is the
coefficient family supported at the zero monomial with value $r$, and the
indeterminate $x_i$ is supported at the exponent family that is $1$ at $i$ and
$0$ elsewhere.

The convolution is well defined and these operations make the displayed set a
commutative ring by [[thm-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-is-a-commutative-ring]].

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Positive-weight transverse product.** Choose the usual rowwise $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ triple. On $\operatorname{Hom}(R_b,R_a)$ the strings have highest $h$-weight $p_a+p_b-2k$, $1\le k\le\min(p_a,p_b)$. Since the pyramid grading element differs from $h$ by row scalars, their highest and lowest grading weights are $2(p_b-k)\ge0$ and $-2(p_a-k)\le0$. Thus the negative-degree part is injected by $\operatorname{ad}e$ and gives the direct-sum complement of [F1]. The differential of $\alpha(u,z)=uzu^{-1}$ at $(1,e)$ is $(x,y)\mapsto[x,e]+y$, an isomorphism. Use weight $-H$ on $\mathfrak m$ and weight $2-H$ on the translated slice and target coordinates; these are positive. In homogeneous coordinates of increasing weight, each component of $\alpha$ is an invertible linear block in the variables of that weight plus a polynomial in lower-weight variables. Successive substitution constructs its polynomial inverse. In particular derivative invertibility alone is not being used as a global inverse theorem.

**Detection.** The shifted operators $x-\chi(x)$ form a representation of the nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak m$, because $\chi$ kills brackets. A nonzero central element has a nonzero kernel on any nonzero locally nilpotent module: apply its largest nonvanishing power to a nonzero vector. That kernel is stable, and the quotient Lie algebra acts on it with the same local nilpotence. Induction on $\dim\mathfrak m$ therefore gives a common nonzero invariant. The case $\mathfrak m=0$ is immediate.

**The actual graded complex.** PBW and [F3] give $\operatorname{gr}Q_\chi=\mathbb C[e+\mathfrak m^\perp]$, with no additional symbol factor. Step 1.1 identifies this with $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]\otimes\mathbb C[S]$. Infinitesimal conjugation acts by invariant vector fields on the first factor and trivially on the slice factor. Giving the exterior dual of a grading-degree $-2r$ vector weight $2r$ makes the twisted Chevalley–Eilenberg differential filtration preserving. Its graded complex is the polynomial de Rham complex of $M_{\mathrm{unip}}$, tensored with $\mathbb C[S]$: invariant vector fields trivialize the tangent bundle and the bracket terms are precisely the de Rham differential. Polynomial exponential coordinates identify this unipotent group with affine space. On a polynomial form of positive total degree $t$, $t^{-1}\iota_{\mathrm{Euler}}$ is a contracting homotopy; constants are the only surviving degree-zero classes.

**Filtered lifting and right freeness.** A positive-degree cocycle in the actual complex has a graded leading term which is a boundary by step 2.1. Lift that boundary and subtract it, strictly lowering the integer filtration degree; boundedness below terminates this process. The same procedure lifts every graded invariant, using vanishing of graded degree-one cohomology to remove its differential. Hence $H^{>0}(\mathfrak m,Q_\chi)=0$ and $\operatorname{gr}W=\mathbb C[S]$, since $H^0(\mathfrak m,Q_\chi)=W$ by the defining invariant realization. Using the fixed PBW vector-space identification $U(\mathfrak p)\to Q_\chi$, take homogeneous coordinate representatives in $U(\mathfrak p)$ and form their ordered products there before projecting to $Q_\chi$. This never multiplies abstract classes in a left-ideal quotient. Their projected ordered monomials, acted on by the right $W$ bimodule action, span $Q_\chi$ by finite descending leading-term subtraction. A finite relation among them would give a relation between distinct monomials over $\operatorname{gr}W$; independence of polynomial monomials rules this out. Thus $Q_\chi$ is right $W$-free. All statements include the independent scalar coordinate of $\mathfrak{gl}_N$.

**Transfer to every module without graded-flatness assumptions.** The finite augmented cochain complex $0\to W\to C^0\to\cdots\to C^{\dim\mathfrak m}\to0$, where $C^j=Q_\chi\otimes\bigwedge^j\mathfrak m^*$, is exact by step 3.1 and is a complex of right $W$-modules. Its differentials are right $W$-linear because the right action commutes with the twisted left $\mathfrak m$ action. Each term is right $W$-free. Starting at the last term, split each surjection onto the already-projective boundary module; descending induction makes every boundary projective and splits every short exact sequence, including $W\hookrightarrow C^0$. These splittings supply a right $W$-linear contraction of the augmented complex. Tensor the contraction with an arbitrary left $W$-module $X$. This remains a contraction, and the resulting complex is exactly the twisted Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of $Q_\chi\otimes_W X$. Consequently its positive cohomology vanishes and its degree-zero cohomology is $X$ via $x\mapsto1_\chi\otimes x$. No filtration or flatness of $X$ is assumed. The splittings use exactly [F4].

The preceding steps prove the three assertions with the doubled even grading. In particular there is no degree $-1$ symplectic or Clifford contribution. If $e=0$, then $\mathfrak m=0$ and the product, augmentation and all cohomology identities reduce to their degree-zero identities.

citations.quote:
Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i,i+1}$), and
$F_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i+1,i}$). For $i<j$, the higher-root
coefficients $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{i,j}$ and
$F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{j,i}$; they are defined recursively by
adjacent-root commutators, not declared as a duplicate independent family.
These generators are subject to the shifted Drinfeld relations of the source (the
shifted analogues of the $D$-$D$, $D$-$E$, $D$-$F$, $E$-$E$, $F$-$F$ and
$E$-$F$ relations, with the shift matrix $\sigma$ entering through the ranges
and the constants). Two filtrations are fixed on it: the **canonical
filtration**, in which each generator of upper index $r$ has degree $r$, and
the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Keep the pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$
of [[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]] and
the finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$, the bimodule $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$
and the Whittaker category of
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Double the pyramid
grading by declaring the degree of $e_{i,j}$ to be
$2(\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i))$; then $e$ has degree $2$ and the
degree $-1$ part of $\mathfrak g$ is zero. Let
$\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r>0,\ r\ \mathrm{even}}\mathfrak g_{-r}$ in the doubled
grading (the strictly negative even part), carrying the character $\chi$. Then:

1. There is a homogeneous transverse complement
   $S=e+\ker(\operatorname{ad} f)$ for a suitable $f\in\mathfrak g$, and the
   conjugation map $M_{\mathrm{unip}}\times S\to e+\mathfrak m^\perp$,
   $(u,s)\mapsto usu^{-1}$, is a polynomial isomorphism; the Kazhdan
   associated graded of $Q_\chi$ is $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]\otimes\mathbb C[S]$
   and $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=\mathbb C[S]$.
2. Assuming the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], for every $W(\lambda)$-module $X$, the twisted $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of
   $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}X$ vanishes in positive degree and its degree-zero
   part is $X$.
3. Every nonzero module on which all $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$, act
   locally nilpotently has a nonzero simultaneous invariant vector; in
   particular $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M$ in the Whittaker
   category.

These assertions use the doubled good grading; no nondegenerate alternating
form on the original degree $-1$ space is asserted.

Let $A$ be a unital algebra with an increasing **multiplicative filtration**

$$0=F_{-1}A\subseteq F_0A\subseteq F_1A\subseteq\cdots,$$

where $1\in F_0A$ and $(F_mA)(F_nA)\subseteq F_{m+n}A$. Its
**associated graded algebra** is

$$\operatorname{gr}_F A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}F_nA/F_{n-1}A,$$

with multiplication on homogeneous classes

$$ (a+F_{m-1}A)(b+F_{n-1}A)=ab+F_{m+n-1}A.$$

This product is well-defined. Indeed, if $a$ changes by
$u\in F_{m-1}A$ and $b$ by $v\in F_{n-1}A$, the product changes by
$ub+av+uv\in F_{m+n-1}A$. Associativity and the unit class descend from $A$.

derivations.claim: **RTT spanning and the actual coproduct.** In the unshifted RTT algebra the commutator of modes $r,s$ has canonical degree at most $r+s-1$, so induction on total degree and the number of unordered pairs rewrites every word into ordered monomials. Matrix-unit brackets verify RTT for $L_a(u)=I+E^{(a)}/u$ in the $a$th factor of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)^{\otimes l}$. Multiplication of RTT matrices with commuting coefficient algebras preserves RTT: moving the two middle commuting tensor factors past each other allows the first RTT identity, then the second. Thus the iterated evaluation map is $T(u)\mapsto L_1(u)\cdots L_l(u)$. More generally shifted evaluation points give the ordered product $\prod_{a=1}^l(I+E^{(a)}/(u-c_a))$, in increasing factor order. Its $u^{-r}$ coefficient when all $c_a=0$ is $\sum_{a_1<\cdots<a_r}E^{(a_1)}\cdots E^{(a_r)}$, homogeneous of enveloping PBW degree $r$.

We first prove invariance of the actual path generators for both column arrangements, independently of generation. For a box a write c(a) for its column, $\rho_c=n-\sum_{d\ge c}q_d$ and $\widetilde E_{ab}=(-1)^{c(b)-c(a)}(E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}\rho_{c(a)})$. The negative PBW projection $\operatorname{pr}:U(\mathfrak g)=U(\mathfrak p)U(\mathfrak m)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ applies χ to the right factor. Its elementary rules are $\operatorname{pr}(ZB)=\chi(Z)B+\operatorname{pr}([Z,B])$ and $\operatorname{pr}(BZ)=B\chi(Z)$ for a negative matrix unit Z and a p-factor B. The bracket is $[\widetilde E_{ab},\widetilde E_{hk}]=\delta_{bh}(\widetilde E_{ak}-\delta_{ak}\rho_{c(a)})-\delta_{ak}(\widetilde E_{hb}-\delta_{hb}\rho_{c(b)})$, and $\chi(\widetilde E_{ab})=-\delta_{\operatorname{row}(a),\operatorname{row}(b)}$ at adjacent negative columns, zero at greater distance. The path sum $P_{ij;x}^{(r)}$ has total degree $\sum(c(b_t)-c(a_t)+1)=r$, p-factors, shared intervening rows, starting/ending rows i,j, strict forward joins when the intervening row exceeds x and weak reverse joins otherwise, and sign $(-1)^{r-s}$ times one minus for every intervening row at most x. Its ηtail image is the same path sum in the displayed shifted factors. Invariance means $\operatorname{pr}([z,\eta_{\rm tail}(P)])=0$. If an element B is invariant, then $(z-\chi(z))B=B(z-\chi(z))+[z,B]$ proves $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi B\subseteq U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$; hence invariant elements form a subalgebra, and products, commutators and coefficients of inverse series with identity constant are invariant.

The local Gan–Ginzburg supplier is stated for the original left-justified diagram; we derive the reflected version by an actual graded Lie isomorphism. Let f reflect boxes, $\tau(E_{ab})=E'_{f(b),f(a)}$ reverse products, and let S on the reflected space be diagonal with $S_{bb}=(-1)^{\operatorname{col}'(b)}$. The linear map $\phi(x)=S(-\tau(x))S^{-1}$ is a Lie isomorphism, because $[\tau(x),\tau(y)]=-\tau([x,y])$. It preserves grading degrees, p and m, and the trace pairing. The diagonal-conjugation sign on every positive adjacent arrow is −1, so $\phi(e)=e'$ and $\chi'\phi=\chi$. It extends to an ALGEBRA isomorphism of enveloping algebras and takes $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ to $U(\mathfrak g')I_{\chi'}$. Thus it takes the entire untwisted left reduction $A=\eta_{\rm tail}(W)$ to $A'$: each defining commutator condition is equivalent under φ. The chart map is the explicit algebra isomorphism $\beta=\eta_{\rm tail}'^{-1}\phi\eta_{\rm tail}:W\to W'$. Scalar translations have smaller positive Kazhdan degree, so $\operatorname{gr}\beta=\operatorname{gr}\phi$. The doubled good grading, sl2 triple, trace-orthogonal slice and transverse product transport under φ. Consequently the proved original polynomial-slice and cohomological statements imply the reflected statements in its actual grading, including the homogeneous coordinate weights. The polynomial-slice part used here is choice-free; for consumers assuming AC as in the cohomological supplier, its left Skryabin quotient, local-nilpotence category, invariant space and equivalence maps also transport first through φ and then through β. This uses the original proved local supplier without enlarging its stated domain, and does not assert that a transpose subalgebra is the whole reflected reduction or that two chart twists act equally on a fixed module.

**Index and inverse sign in the abstract quotient.** Write $A_i(u)=D_i(u)^{-1}=\sum_{t\ge0}A_i^{(t)}u^{-t}$, so $A_i^{(0)}=1$, while the defining relation uses $\widetilde D_i(u)=-A_i(u)$ with constant $-1$. Thus $[E_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)}]=-D_{i+1}^{(a+b-1)}-\sum_{t=1}^{a+b-1}A_i^{(t)}D_{i+1}^{(a+b-1-t)}$. Put $i=c-1$, $u=s_{c-1,c}$, $v=s_{c,c-1}$, $a=r-v$, $b=v+1$. Then $a+b-1=r$ and $D_c^{(r)}=-\sum_{t=1}^rA_{c-1}^{(t)}D_c^{(r-t)}-[E_{c-1}^{(r-v)},F_{c-1}^{(v+1)}]$. We use this only for $r>p_c=p_{c-1}+u+v$, so $a>p_{c-1}+u$ is an allowed but HIGH E mode, to be eliminated before the diagonal formula is used. Also $A_i^{(r)}=-\sum_{t=1}^rD_i^{(t)}A_i^{(r-t)}$, giving polynomial inverse coefficients with the same canonical degree bound. This derives the sign and indices, rather than treating a negative inverse as a positive one.

**Product Jacobian and independence.** Let $l$ be at least the largest coefficient index in a proposed relation. In the commutative symbol algebra of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)^{\otimes l}$ write $P_r(X_1,\ldots,X_l)=\sum_{a_1<\cdots<a_r}X_{a_1}\cdots X_{a_r}$. At $X_a=h_aI$, with nonzero pairwise distinct $h_a$, the differential on every matrix entry is $dP_r=\sum_a e_{r-1}(h_1,\ldots,\widehat{h_a},\ldots,h_l)dX_a$. The column coefficient polynomials $\prod_{b\ne a}(1+h_bz)$ are linearly independent, since evaluating at $z=-1/h_c$ leaves only column $c$, with a nonzero value. Hence the Jacobian is invertible. A polynomial relation of minimal total degree, differentiated and multiplied by the inverse Jacobian over the rational function field, makes each of its partial derivatives a lower-degree relation; minimality and characteristic zero force the relation to be constant and zero. Thus the coordinates $P_{r,ij}$, $1\le r\le l$, are algebraically independent. A highest weighted-degree part of an enveloping relation among their ordered lifts would contradict this polynomial independence by [F2]. This proves RTT PBW for all modes. The $h_a$ are scalar-matrix points in the symbol space, independently of spectral evaluation parameters.

Group equal row lengths into the minimal admissible parabolic blocks ν, with final nonempty block m of size t. D/E/F below are its actual Gauss path coefficients. Deleting the last column embeds the smaller shifted matrix units into the current ones; on unshifted diagonal units this compensates the rho difference by a scalar translation, and on negative units it preserves χ. A dot denotes the smaller coefficients. With final column A, preceding column B, $L_{kj}=\widetilde E_{(A,k),(A,j)}$ and $C_{hj}=\widetilde E_{(B,h),(A,j)}$, the right end recursions, for any fixed bottom row h, are $D_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot D_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}(\sum_k\dot D_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}+[\dot D_{a;ih}^{(r-1)},C_{hj}])$, $E_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot E_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}(\sum_k\dot E_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}+[\dot E_{a;ih}^{(r-1)},C_{hj}])$, and $F_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot F_{a;ij}^{(r)}$. The E boundary formula is used for r>1. Deleting the FIRST column of the reflected arrangement has the ordinary embedding on the remaining shifted factors. With first column A, next B, $L_{ik}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(A,k)}$ and $C_{ih}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(B,h)}$, its LEFT recursions are $D_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot D_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}(\sum_kL_{ik}\dot D_{a;kj}^{(r-1)}+[C_{ih},\dot D_{a;hj}^{(r-1)}])$, $E_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot E_{a;ij}^{(r)}$, and $F_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot F_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}(\sum_kL_{ik}\dot F_{a;kj}^{(r-1)}+[C_{ih},\dot F_{a;hj}^{(r-1)}])$, with r>1 in the F boundary formula. To verify these identities, cut each path at its final or initial visit to the added column. Paths missing that column give the dotted coefficient; paths ending or starting in its block give the product sum. For a crossing path the two neighboring cut positions at the common bottom row h have opposite signs and give the two orders in the commutator; further visits pair by moving to the neighboring cut. The identical cut rule in a changed row interval proves the Gauss identities: paths without an intermediate visit occur once; paths with such a visit have the two neighboring cuts with opposite sign. Thus these are identities for the actual Gauss coefficients. In particular LEFT deletion corrects F and leaves E unchanged; it does not use the interchanged E/F display in the source.

**Finite spanning: earlier blocks and boundary E/F.** In the abstract quotient by $D_1^{(r)}$, $r>p_1$, let $\Omega_c$ contain D modes $1\le a\le c$, $1\le r\le p_a$, E roots $a<b\le c$, $s_{ab}<r\le s_{ab}+p_a$, and F roots $a<b\le c$, $s_{ba}<r\le s_{ba}+p_a$; let $B_c$ be their algebra. Induct on c to show every allowed mode with endpoints at most c belongs to $B_c$ with total canonical degree at most its index. The case c=1 is the imposed truncation, including $p_1=0$. For the inductive step put $u=s_{c-1,c}$ and $v=s_{c,c-1}$. For $r>u+p_{c-1}$, the D–E relation gives $E_{c-1}^{(r)}=[D_{c-1}^{(r-u)},E_{c-1}^{(u+1)}]-\sum_{t=1}^{r-u-1}D_{c-1}^{(t)}E_{c-1}^{(r-t)}$. The bracket of an earlier finite diagonal mode of index a with the lowest boundary E gives terms $D^{(t)}E_{c-1}^{(a+u-t)}$ with $a\le p_{c-1}$ in the only nonzero diagonal block, hence new E indices at most $u+p_{c-1}$. An earlier finite root $E_{b,c-1}^{(a)}$ gives $E_{b,c}^{(a+u)}$ and any block-refinement split terms, all with $a+u\le s_{b,c-1}+p_b+u=s_{b,c}+p_b$. Earlier negative roots and earlier positive roots without endpoint $c-1$ commute with the lowest boundary E. Thus the expanded commutator is in $B_c$. In the sum $u+1\le r-t<r$, so induction on r reduces those E modes; all products have degree at most r. The reversed D–F relation and reversed product orders give the same argument with boundary bound $v+p_{c-1}$.

**Gauss and shifted PBW.** Coefficientwise formal inversion and $T=FDE$ give mutually inverse polynomial changes between RTT and Gauss coordinates: the Gauss mode of index $r$ equals the corresponding RTT coordinate plus expressions in smaller mode indices of total canonical degree $r$. The shifted Drinfeld relations straighten shifted root-mode words, with lower canonical-degree commutator corrections; the adjacent root commutator definitions and Serre relations perform the higher-root straightening. Their RTT images have the same Gauss symbols in the allowed shifted ranges. Those symbols form an independent subset of the polynomial coordinate system, so these spanning words are independent and the shifted presentation embeds. Thus its canonical associated graded is precisely the polynomial algebra on its allowed root symbols. This argument concerns the untruncated algebra; it does not infer independence after quotienting.

Induct on the number of columns, deleting the last column in the original left-justified diagram and the first in the reflected diagram. Steps 3.2, 4.1, 5.1, 4.2 and 5.2 cover every allowed parabolic D/E/F mode for the original and reflected arrangements. Refining a minimal block is its formal Gauss decomposition: coefficients of its inverse and resulting factors are polynomials in its previous coefficients, hence invariant by step 1.2. This gives all ordinary simple modes; higher-root commutator definitions give all higher roots. Therefore the actual untwisted-chart images $P_{ii;i-1}^{(r)},P_{i,i+1;i}^{(r)},P_{i+1,i;i}^{(r)}$ and all their higher-root polynomials belong to their actual left reductions. This conclusion covers the infinite allowed mode families and does not rely on finite generation, finite truncation or a reflected W identification.

**Finite Levi Jacobian.** Project $U(\mathfrak p)$ to its column Levi enveloping algebra and take canonical symbols. At its diagonal point $X_c=h_cI$, let $Q_i(z)=\prod_{c\le p_i}(1+h_cz)$. The diagonal D first variations are $z\prod_{a\le p_i,a\ne c}(1+h_az)$. For $i<j$, set $m=p_i$, $M=p_j$. A first variation in a common column $c\le m$ has just one off-diagonal factor. Summing the same-column negative-cut repeats and the strictly increasing positive-cut visits in the path formula gives $dE_{ij}(z)=z\prod_{a=m+1}^M(1+h_az)/(1+h_cz)$ and $dF_{ji}(z)=z/(1+h_cz)$ on that entry. These are identities for the allowed coefficient derivatives, not an identification of excluded low product coefficients with shifted generators. Their coefficients in modes $M-m+k$ and $k$, $1\le k\le m$, are respectively $(-h_c)^{k-1}\prod_{a=m+1}^M(h_a-h_c)$ and $(-h_c)^{k-1}$. For higher roots, the canonical symbol of the adjacent root commutator is the Levi Lie–Poisson bracket. At $X_c=h_cI$ this Poisson tensor is zero, so the differential of a bracket uses only the two first differentials and the differential of the Poisson tensor. With $i<k<j$ and $p_k=t$, the coefficients from $E_{ik}^{(r-s_{kj})}$ and $E_{kj}^{(s_{kj}+1)}$ multiply to $(-h_c)^{a-1}\prod_{m<b\le t}(h_b-h_c)\prod_{t<b\le M}(h_b-h_c)$ when $r=M-m+a$, since $\{X_{c,ik},X_{c,kj}\}=X_{c,ij}$. For F the reversed recursion uses $\{X_{c,jk},X_{c,ki}\}=X_{c,ji}$, with coefficients one and $(-h_c)^{r-1}$. Thus induction gives the displayed first variations for all higher roots as well. Choose the $h_c$ nonzero and pairwise distinct. Each row-pair block is Vandermonde with nonzero column factors; each diagonal block is the elementary-symmetric Jacobian from step 2.1. Different row pairs use disjoint entry variables, so the full Jacobian has rank $\sum_{ij}\min(p_i,p_j)$. The corresponding finite symbols are algebraically independent by step 2.1's differentiation argument. Reflection reverses column order and interchanges E and F, giving the same invertible blocks with transposed shifts. Empty rows contribute zero-sized blocks.

**The whole reduction is generated.** Write $\mathcal W$ for the entire quantum Hamiltonian reduction, before any identification with a Yangian quotient. By [F3] its homogeneous Hilbert series is $H(t)=\prod_{i,j}\prod_{r=s_{ij}+1}^{s_{ij}+\min(p_i,p_j)}(1-t^r)^{-1}$. Each weight is positive, so every coefficient is finite. Step 6.1 places every ordered finite-generator monomial of total degree at most $d$ inside $F_d^K\mathcal W$. Step 7.1 and enveloping PBW make these monomials independent: a highest-degree relation after Levi projection would give a polynomial relation among the independent symbols. Their number is exactly $\sum_{k\le d}[t^k]H(t)$, which is also $\dim F_d^K\mathcal W$ by [F3] for the original pair and step 1.3 for the reflected pair. Thus their span equals $F_d^K\mathcal W$ for every $d$. Exhaustivity proves generation of the entire reduction and its ordered filtered basis, and also injectivity of the Levi projection on that entire algebra. The same homogeneous dimension equality proves full generation for the reflected reduction using its own allowed modes and transposed shifts. This uses the Gan–Ginzburg slice theorem independently of W-PBW, not just generic independence in a restricted subalgebra.

**Relations, finite order and the whole-algebra identification.** The end path identities prove the shifted coefficient relations and the $D_1$ cutoff on the invariant representatives. One can check them after Levi projection, now injective on the entire reduction by step 8.1: the right end images are $D_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot D_a^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}\sum_k\dot D_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}$, $E_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot E_a^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}\sum_k\dot E_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}$, and $F_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot F_a^{(r)}$; the left versions place L before the dotted coefficients and correct F instead. Substitute these finite coefficient expressions in each D–D, D–E, D–F, E–F, equal-root and adjacent-root relation. Terms with no L give the smaller relation. Terms with one L give the smaller D-weight relation; terms with two L use $[L_{ij},L_{hk}]=\delta_{jh}L_{ik}-\delta_{ki}L_{hj}$. The inverse-D convolution cancels paired split coefficients, and the adjacent triple relations group into those same terms and the matrix Jacobi identity. Hence the relations hold by column induction, starting with matrix-unit brackets at one column; injectivity lifts them back to the actual reduction. For D1 the cutoff row interval is empty, so every join is strictly forward; a path beginning and ending in row1 satisfies $r=\sum(c(b_t)-c(a_t)+1)\le c(b_s)-c(a_1)+1\le p_1$. Thus the smallest-row path has no coefficient above $p_1$, giving the actual $D_1$ cutoff in either arrangement. There is therefore a homomorphism from the abstract truncated quotient onto the invariant-generated whole algebra. Steps 2.3 and 3.3 give finite spanning; commutator swapping lowers canonical degree, so induction on that degree and the number of unordered pairs straightens these finite expressions into ordered $\Omega_n$ monomials. Their images are the independent ordered reduction basis of step 8.1, so the homomorphism is injective as well. This proves the quotient presentation and the finite Gauss PBW basis without restricting an infinite basis through a quotient.

The full generator theorem just proved for BOTH arrangements now identifies the original head/right model. With the reflected-box anti-map τ from step 1.3, send a path $(a_1,b_1),\ldots,(a_s,b_s)$ to $(f(b_s),f(a_s)),\ldots,(f(b_1),f(a_1))$. Each displacement is unchanged. A reversed join compares $l+1-c(a_{k+1})$ with $l+1-c(b_k)$, so its strict-forward or weak-reverse rule is exactly the original one; its row is $\operatorname{row}(a_{k+1})=\operatorname{row}(b_k)$, preserving its sign. Total degree, number of factors and total sign are identical; the product order is precisely τ's reversal. This involutive bijection proves $\tau(P_{ij;x}^{(r)})=P_{ji;x}^{\prime(r)}$ for ALL i,j,x and modes r, including the diagonal constants at r=0. In particular τ exchanges simple E/F images and fixes the corresponding D images, transposing the shift matrix and preserving mode number. Since these explicit images generate each WHOLE reduction by step 8.1, both inclusions give $\tau(W)=W'$, rather than only the image of a path subalgebra.

The preceding construction applies to both directional shift matrices, using the corresponding left or right end formulas in step 9.1. Thus it proves the full finite quotient basis, equality with the whole reduction, and strict canonical/Kazhdan filtration in both arrangements. Its degree-r homogeneous basis is the monomial basis counted by the exact slice Hilbert series, and the projection used for the relation check is injective on the entire reduction. These are the prerequisites for the original right-normalizer identification below.

**Actual original prefix coefficient identity.** Let $\lambda_m$ be the first m columns of the decreasing-column pyramid, $I=I_{m-1}:U(\mathfrak g_{m-1})\hookrightarrow U(\mathfrak g_m)$ the ordinary UNSHIFTED box embedding, and $b_a(j)$ the box in row j and column a when it exists. Put negative-index coefficients zero and $T_{ij}^{(0)}=\delta_{ij}$. The original coefficient recursion, for r>0, is $T_{ij}^{(r)}(\lambda_m)=I(T_{ij}^{(r)})-\sum_{h\le n-q_m,\ s_{hj}\le r}I(T_{ih}^{(r-s_{hj})})I(T_{hj}^{(s_{hj})})+\sum_{h>n-q_m}I(T_{ih}^{(r-1)})E_{b_m(h),b_m(j)}-[I(T_{ij}^{(r-1)}),E_{b_{m-1}(j),b_m(j)}]$, where coefficients inside I belong to $\lambda_{m-1}$ and shifts in the sum belong to $\lambda_m$. The final THREE terms are omitted for $j\le n-q_m$, and a nonexistent box omits its term. To derive the identity before any cutoff is known, apply the right end identities to the last Gauss block in the ordinary chart. D has its smaller D plus its last-column Levi product and minus its previous-to-last bridge commutator; E has the same two corrections and starts with the smaller $\bar E$. The precise smaller-block subtraction is $\bar E_{a,b}(u)=E_{a,b}(u)-\sum_{c=a}^{b-1}E_{a,c}(u)E_{c,b}^{(\dot s_{cb}+1)}u^{-\dot s_{cb}-1}$, all in the smaller diagram. For a shorter block c and last block b, $\dot s_{cb}+1=s_{cb}$. Insert these expressions into $T_{ij}(u)=\sum(F_{c,a}(u)D_c(u)E_{c,b}(u))_{ij}$. Unchanged terms give the first embedded T; the $\bar E$ subtractions group by shorter terminal row h into the product with split $(r-s_{hj},s_{hj})$; the L products group into the Levi sum. Leibniz groups the common bridge into the displayed single commutator. Higher-root end identities follow by their adjacent recursion; its earlier-block factor has no terminal bridge endpoint, so its bracket with that bridge is zero. This proves the prefix identity itself and retains its actual coefficient index.

**Loop symbols and the two graded algebras.** In the unshifted RTT relation the top loop-degree commutator is the current matrix-unit bracket; terms with two positive-index factors have smaller loop degree. Gauss multiplication changes a mode of index $r$ by products of at least two factors of total canonical index $r$, hence smaller loop degree than $r-1$. Taking the shifted root relations gives the same brackets with allowed current modes $e_{ij}t^a$, $a\ge s_{ij}$; shift additivity makes their span a Lie subalgebra. The ordered basis of step 3.1 is a filtered basis also for intrinsic loop degree, because loop straightening never raises total degree and independence of the full ordered words rules out a lower-degree expression. Current PBW uses only finite-dimensional PBW: any proposed relation uses finitely many modes, and a jet quotient with larger cutoff preserves those basis vectors and makes their enveloping monomials independent. Hence the loop associated graded is $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n[t](\sigma))$. Canonical degree instead gave a commutative polynomial algebra. For the finite reduction the Kazhdan associated graded is the commutative slice algebra from step 8.1, while the leading single-factor terms of the finite generators lie in the actual centralizer $\mathfrak g^e\subseteq\mathfrak p$; the next theorem identifies the loop graded algebra by ambient enveloping PBW. Noncommutativity distinguishes the two graded algebras whenever the corresponding Lie algebra is nonabelian.

**Every coefficient above the bound is zero.** For the original decreasing-column diagram $S_{ij}=s_{ij}+\min(p_i,p_j)=p_j$ for EVERY ordered row pair. Induct on the column count m using step 10.2; the one-column T has no coefficient above one directly. An empty row contributes only a diagonal constant. If $j\le n-q_m$, its row length is unchanged on removal, so the only embedded T term vanishes for $r>p_j$ by induction. If j is a bottom row, $p_j=m$, and the first embedded T vanishes for $r>m$ because its smaller target-row length is m−1. In each shorter-row product, $p_h$ is unchanged and $s_{hj}=m-p_h$, so $r-s_{hj}>p_h=S_{ih}(\lambda_{m-1})$ for ANY i, killing its first factor. In the Levi sum every h has smaller row length m−1, and $r-1>m-1=S_{ih}(\lambda_{m-1})$ kills its coefficient. The same inequality kills the T coefficient inside the final commutator. This covers every term, including the boundary $r=m+1$, and proves $T_{ij}^{(r)}=0$ for $r>S_{ij}$. The lower zero range $0<r\le s_{ij}$ follows coefficientwise from FDE and shift additivity. No truncation fact was assumed to prove itself.

**Finite T coordinates and loop symbols.** Coefficientwise FDE and Gauss inversion are weighted triangular in the original index r: the mode equals its corresponding Gauss coordinate plus products of smaller mode indices of total canonical degree r. The finite Gauss eliminations from steps 2.3 and 3.3 and the actual cutoff in step 11.2 close both inversions on exactly the finite set. Thus these finite canonical symbols are another polynomial coordinate system, and the ordered finite T monomials have the same filtered basis as the Gauss monomials in step 9.1, in any prescribed order. A signed path term with k factors and coefficient index r has ambient good degree at most r−k; scalar replacements lower it further. Only its single-factor part contributes in degree r−1, giving $(-1)^{r-1}\sum_{\operatorname{row}(a)=i,\operatorname{row}(b)=j,\ c(b)-c(a)=r-1}E_{ab}=(-1)^{r-1}e_{ij;r-1}$. Products introduced by Gauss inversion have at least two factors and smaller good degree. This proves the symbol dictionary with the existing coefficient index and no spectral rescaling.

Put $\eta_{\rm head}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{d\le c(a)}q_d)$. This and ηtail are algebra automorphisms: a matrix bracket can have diagonal part only from $E_{ab},E_{ba}\in\mathfrak p$, which forces equal columns and equal diagonal shifts, so the scalar functional kills the commutator; the negative scalar translation is the inverse. Reflection gives $\sum_{d\ge c'(f(a))}q'_d=\sum_{d\le c(a)}q_d$, hence $\tau\eta_{\rm head}=\eta'_{\rm tail}\tau$. Also $\tau(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m'$, $\chi'\tau=\chi$ by the trace calculation, and $\tau(I_\chi U(\mathfrak g))=U(\mathfrak g')I_{\chi'}$, since τ reverses products and sends each shifted negative generator to its reflected one. Therefore $\tau([\eta_{\rm head}(u),x])=[\tau(x),\eta'_{\rm tail}(\tau(u))]$. Bijectivity shows that u satisfies the ORIGINAL head/right condition exactly when τ(u) belongs to the reflected LEFT reduction. Step 9.2 identifies its inverse image with the original W, proving BOTH inclusions in $W=\{u:[\eta_{\rm head}(u),\mathfrak m]\subseteq I_\chi U(\mathfrak g)\}$. The induced Gauss transpose also satisfies $\tau(T_{ij}^{(r)})=T_{ji}^{\prime(r)}$: apply the coefficientwise reversed FDE factors and their Gauss cut identities. Thus step 11.2 gives the reflected upper cutoff $r>S_{ji}=S_{ij}^{\prime}$, with the same finite triangular T basis. This proves right invariance for every original shifted generator, higher-root mode and product, beyond the numerical identity $\eta_{\rm head}-\eta_{\rm tail}=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak m}\operatorname{ad}$.

Write $J_L=U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ and $J_R=I_\chi U(\mathfrak g)$. The identities $(x-\chi(x))\eta_{\rm tail}(w)=\eta_{\rm tail}(w)(x-\chi(x))+[x,\eta_{\rm tail}(w)]$ and $\eta_{\rm head}(w)(x-\chi(x))=(x-\chi(x))\eta_{\rm head}(w)+[\eta_{\rm head}(w),x]$ prove $J_L\eta_{\rm tail}(w)\subseteq J_L$ and $\eta_{\rm head}(w)J_R\subseteq J_R$ for every w∈W. Thus $Q_L=U(\mathfrak g)/J_L$ has its actual right action $\overline a\cdot w=\overline{a\eta_{\rm tail}(w)}$, and $Q_R=U(\mathfrak g)/J_R$ its actual left action $w\cdot\overline a=\overline{\eta_{\rm head}(w)a}$, commuting with the respective enveloping actions by associativity. These are module quotients, not quotient rings. Right Whittaker vectors act by $v\cdot w=v\eta_{\rm head}(w)$ because they annihilate J_R. Turning a right U(g)-module into a left reflected module by $a'v=v\tau^{-1}(a')$ identifies its right Whittaker space and W action with the reflected left ones, using $\tau^{-1}\eta'_{\rm tail}\tau=\eta_{\rm head}$. For consumers assuming AC, transporting their proved left Skryabin equivalence through the reflected Lie isomorphism in step 1.3 and then this anti-map gives the right equivalence with inverse $-\otimes_WQ_R$; that conditional categorical assertion is separate from the choice-free algebra identity. Every action is the explicit original or reflected chart action; no equality of different twists on an arbitrary fixed representation is assumed.

citations.quote:
Keep the pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$
of [[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]] and
the finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$, the bimodule $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$
and the Whittaker category of
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Double the pyramid
grading by declaring the degree of $e_{i,j}$ to be
$2(\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i))$; then $e$ has degree $2$ and the
degree $-1$ part of $\mathfrak g$ is zero. Let
$\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r>0,\ r\ \mathrm{even}}\mathfrak g_{-r}$ in the doubled
grading (the strictly negative even part), carrying the character $\chi$. Then:

1. There is a homogeneous transverse complement
   $S=e+\ker(\operatorname{ad} f)$ for a suitable $f\in\mathfrak g$, and the
   conjugation map $M_{\mathrm{unip}}\times S\to e+\mathfrak m^\perp$,
   $(u,s)\mapsto usu^{-1}$, is a polynomial isomorphism; the Kazhdan
   associated graded of $Q_\chi$ is $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]\otimes\mathbb C[S]$
   and $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=\mathbb C[S]$.
2. Assuming the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], for every $W(\lambda)$-module $X$, the twisted $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of
   $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}X$ vanishes in positive degree and its degree-zero
   part is $X$.
3. Every nonzero module on which all $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$, act
   locally nilpotently has a nonzero simultaneous invariant vector; in
   particular $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M$ in the Whittaker
   category.

These assertions use the doubled good grading; no nondegenerate alternating
form on the original degree $-1$ space is asserted.

Keep the type-A pyramid data
$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], with
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism
with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a Lie algebra over $k$. In $T(\mathfrak g)$, regard
$[x,y]\in\mathfrak g$ as an element of tensor degree one, and let $I$ be the
two-sided ideal generated by

$$x\otimes y-y\otimes x-[x,y]\qquad(x,y\in\mathfrak g).$$

The **universal enveloping algebra** is

$$U(\mathfrak g)=T(\mathfrak g)/I.$$

Write

$$\iota_{\mathfrak g}:\mathfrak g\longrightarrow U(\mathfrak g)$$

for the composite of the degree-one inclusion with the quotient map. This
definition makes $U(\mathfrak g)$ a unital associative algebra and $\iota_{\mathfrak g}$ a
linear map. It does not assert that $\iota_{\mathfrak g}$ is injective; that conclusion will
come from PBW.

For a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ over $k$ and a $\mathfrak g$-module $M$,
the degree-$n$ **Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains** are

$$C^n(\mathfrak g,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Lambda^n\mathfrak g,M)\quad(n\geq0).$$

Set $C^n(\mathfrak g,M)=0$ for $n<0$. Since
$\Lambda^0\mathfrak g=k$, evaluation at $1$ identifies
$C^0(\mathfrak g,M)$ with $M$. Cochains may equivalently be viewed as
alternating $n$-linear maps $\mathfrak g^n\to M$. No finite-dimensionality
or characteristic hypothesis is needed. If $n>\dim\mathfrak g$ in the
finite-dimensional case, the exterior power and hence the cochain space are
zero.

For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$ and a short exact sequence
$0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ of $\mathfrak g$-modules, the induced CE
complexes form a degreewise short exact sequence and yield the natural long
exact sequence

$$\cdots\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M')\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M)\to H^n(\mathfrak g,M'')\to H^{n+1}(\mathfrak g,M')\to\cdots.$$

Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, so that $l=p_n$ is the number
of columns, and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$
is in bijection with $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$ via
$(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$, and
$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$
and $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This
grading is the type-A pyramid good grading of the source, not the Dynkin
grading attached to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple.

All matrix spaces below carry the commutator bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$ and are
Lie subalgebras of $\mathfrak{gl}_m(\mathbb C)=M_m(\mathbb C)$ in the sense of
[[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]; closure under the bracket is verified in
each case by the computation displayed.

* The **general linear Lie algebra** $\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)=M_n(\mathbb C)$,
  for $n\ge1$. The **special linear Lie algebra**
  $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb C)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):\operatorname{tr}A=0\}$
  is a Lie subalgebra because $\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$, and
  $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ agrees with
  [[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]].
* The **symplectic Lie algebra** $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ is the set of
  $A\in M_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ with $AJ+JA^{T}=0$, for $n\ge1$, where
  $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\-I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$.
* The **orthogonal Lie algebras** $\mathfrak{so}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ and

$A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&-a^{T}\end{pmatrix}$ for the symplectic and even
orthogonal cases, with $b,c$ symmetric for $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$ and
$b,c$ skew-symmetric for $\mathfrak{so}_{2n}(\mathbb C)$, and gives
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&u&-w^{T}\\ w&a&b\\ -u^{T}&c&-a^{T}\end{pmatrix},\qquad u\in M_{1\times n}(\mathbb C),\quad w\in M_{n\times1}(\mathbb C),\quad b,c\ \text{skew-symmetric},$$

derivations.claim: Unit and counit. The adjunction between $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ and $\mathrm{Wh}$ has the unit $u_M\colon M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)$ and counit $c_M\colon Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$ of [F2]. For every $M$, the kernel and cokernel of $u_M$ and $c_M$ lie in the kernel of the invariants functor: applying $H^0$ to the unit and using the vanishing of [F1] identifies the composite with the identity; a short exact sequence argument with the long exact sequence of [F3] then shows that if $H^0$ of a map in the category is an isomorphism then the map is an isomorphism, since the kernel and cokernel have vanishing invariants and a nonzero object of the category has nonzero invariants by [F1]. Hence $u_M,c_M$ are isomorphisms and the two functors are quasi-inverse.

Exactness and detection. Exactness of $\mathrm{Wh}$ follows because it is inverse to the exact functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ (tensoring with the right flat module $Q_\chi$, whose flatness is part of the free right-module structure of the source), and the detection statement is the case $H^0=0$ of [F1].

The transported tensor functor. For $M\in W(\lambda)$-mod and finite-dimensional $X$, the functor $M\mapsto\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ is exact in $M$ because the composed functors are exact; it is the transport of $?\otimes X$ across the equivalence.

**Triangularity of the displayed tensor map.** Keep the polynomial-coordinate/distribution pairing from the good-grading calculation: the right-free PBW coordinates identify $Q_\chi\otimes_W M$ with the locally nilpotent coinduced model, by finite weighted Taylor pairing and descending leading-term subtraction, followed by filtered unions. Cofree evaluation on Whittaker vectors of this model tensored with $X$ gives a vector-space isomorphism $\ell:M\otimes X\to\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_W M)\otimes X)$. It is not the inverse of the displayed $\mu_{M,X}$ in general. Choose a common Engel flag $0=X_0\subset X_1\subset\cdots\subset X_t=X$ for the nilpotent $\mathfrak m$ action, so $\mathfrak m X_j\subset X_{j-1}$; a negative-graded Lie algebra acts nilpotently on a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module. The matrix-coefficient construction of $\ell$ preserves this flag and has diagonal $1_\chi\otimes m\otimes x_j$: on each flag quotient the $\mathfrak m$ action is trivial, and the inverse cofree evaluation is precisely the unit $m\mapsto1_\chi\otimes m$. Every correction term involves a strictly flag-lowering matrix coefficient. PBW represents these finitely supported lifts by elements of $U(\mathfrak p)$ acting on $M$; no completion of $M$ is used. The displayed map applies $\eta^{-1}$ of this representative to $M$ and leaves the $X$ component in its flag position. Thus $A=\mu_{M,X}\ell$ preserves $M\otimes X_j$ and is the identity on its successive quotients. Write $A=1+N$; then $N^t=0$, although its off-diagonal entries can be arbitrary operators on $M$. Hence $A^{-1}=\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}(-N)^r$, and $\mu_{M,X}$ is a vector-space isomorphism. This argument distinguishes cofree constant evaluation from the extension-dependent displayed map.

Associativity. The associativity isomorphisms of the transported functor are obtained by inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms of the tensor product of $\mathfrak g$-modules into the definition of $\circledast$ and applying the inverse equivalence; they are compatible by the naturality of the unit and counit of the adjunction and by the coherence of the tensor associativity in $\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

**Balancing and $W$-linearity.** PBW gives unique representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$, $u\in U(\mathfrak p)$, in $Q_\chi$. Define $\psi_M(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)=um$. Since the right action of $w\in W\subset U(\mathfrak p)$ sends this representative to $\eta(uw)1_\chi$, the formula is right-$W$-balanced: $(uw)m=u(wm)$. Moreover $\psi_M(\eta(v)q\otimes m)=v\psi_M(q\otimes m)$ for $v\in U(\mathfrak p)$. The shift $\eta$ adds a Lie character on $\mathfrak p$, so on its primitive generators, and hence multiplicatively on $U(\mathfrak p)$, $(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(v)=\Delta\eta(v)$. The $W$ action on the source Whittaker subspace is therefore $\Delta\eta(w)$, while the target restricted $\mathfrak p$-module $M\otimes X$ has action $\Delta(w)$. Applying $\psi_M\otimes\mathrm{id}$ to the displayed coproduct identity proves $\mu_{M,X}(wz)=w\mu_{M,X}(z)$. Together with step 2.1 this proves the actual stated $W$-module isomorphism. No equality with cofree evaluation or citation-only character-equation argument is used.

Independence of the order. For $X=V^{\otimes d}$ the isomorphism $\mu_d$ is the composite of the single-step maps $\mu_{\bullet,V}$; two different parenthesizations differ by the associativity isomorphisms of step 2.2, and both are restrictions of the balanced evaluation maps of step 3.1, applied with the same iterated coproduct on $U(\mathfrak p)$; coassociativity and the displayed shift identity make these maps equal. Therefore the resulting isomorphism $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

For any fixed order on the shifted Drinfeld generators and on the root modes of
$Y_n(\sigma)$, their ordered monomials form a $\mathbb C$-basis of
$Y_n(\sigma)$. Its canonical associated graded algebra is the polynomial
algebra on the corresponding symbols, while its loop associated graded algebra
is the universal enveloping algebra of the current algebra
$\mathfrak{gl}_n[t](\sigma)$; the two graded algebras are different and
non-isomorphic in general. In the finite quotient $W(\lambda)$ the ordered
monomials in the finite Gauss range
$$s_{i,j}<r\le s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$$
form a basis, and the commutative Kazhdan/canonical associated graded and the
noncommutative loop associated graded are distinct. Equivalently, the finite
$T$-coefficients with $s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}$ form an ordered PBW basis, where
$r$ is the unshifted coefficient index of $T=FDE$, not a reindexed value.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i,i+1}$), and
$F_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i+1,i}$). For $i<j$, the higher-root
coefficients $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{i,j}$ and
$F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{j,i}$; they are defined recursively by
adjacent-root commutators, not declared as a duplicate independent family.
These generators are subject to the shifted Drinfeld relations of the source (the
shifted analogues of the $D$-$D$, $D$-$E$, $D$-$F$, $E$-$E$, $F$-$F$ and
$E$-$F$ relations, with the shift matrix $\sigma$ entering through the ranges
and the constants). Two filtrations are fixed on it: the **canonical
filtration**, in which each generator of upper index $r$ has degree $r$, and
the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i,i+1}$), and
$F_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i+1,i}$). For $i<j$, the higher-root
coefficients $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{i,j}$ and
$F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{j,i}$; they are defined recursively by

the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, so that $l=p_n$ is the number
of columns, and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$
is in bijection with $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$ via
$(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$, and
$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$
and $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This
grading is the type-A pyramid good grading of the source, not the Dynkin
grading attached to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Let $A$ be a unital algebra with an increasing **multiplicative filtration**

$$0=F_{-1}A\subseteq F_0A\subseteq F_1A\subseteq\cdots,$$

where $1\in F_0A$ and $(F_mA)(F_nA)\subseteq F_{m+n}A$. Its
**associated graded algebra** is

$$\operatorname{gr}_F A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}F_nA/F_{n-1}A,$$

with multiplication on homogeneous classes

$$ (a+F_{m-1}A)(b+F_{n-1}A)=ab+F_{m+n-1}A.$$

This product is well-defined. Indeed, if $a$ changes by
$u\in F_{m-1}A$ and $b$ by $v\in F_{n-1}A$, the product changes by
$ub+av+uv\in F_{m+n-1}A$. Associativity and the unit class descend from $A$.

Keep the type-A pyramid data
$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], with
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism
with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

derivations.claim: **Actual ambient leading term.** Give a matrix unit $e_{a,b}\in\mathfrak p$ its good degree $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)$. In the explicit signed path formula a term of canonical degree $r+1$ with $k$ matrix-unit factors has good degree at most $r+1-k$; a diagonal scalar replacement only lowers that degree. Therefore only single-factor terms contribute in good degree $r$. Those terms sum to $(-1)^r\sum e_{a,b}$ over $\operatorname{row}(a)=i$, $\operatorname{row}(b)=j$, $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)=r$, namely $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. Products introduced by Gauss factorization or its inverse have at least two factors and have smaller good degree. Thus the leading homogeneous component of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ in the actual graded algebra $U(\mathfrak p)$ is exactly $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. This proves the leading-symbol claim using the path degrees rather than a claim that Gauss inversion alone supplies its sign.

**Independence in the ambient enveloping algebra.** The elements $e_{i,j;r}$ form a homogeneous basis of the actual Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak g^e\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Extend that finite basis to a homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak p$, with an order extending the prescribed order of the centralizer basis. Enveloping PBW implies that the ordered monomials in the $e_{i,j;r}$ are linearly independent in $U(\mathfrak p)$, and that the natural homomorphism $U(\mathfrak g^e)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ is injective. Their products and brackets are the actual ambient products and brackets, including all boundary terms of the centralizer strings. No projection of a current bracket with an arbitrary out-of-range convention is needed.

**Strictness of the loop basis.** The finite $T$ monomials form a vector-space basis of $W(\lambda)$ by [F1]. For a monomial with total loop degree $d$, step 1.1 says that its degree-$d$ homogeneous component in $U(\mathfrak p)$ is, up to the product of its displayed signs, the corresponding PBW monomial in $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. In any nonzero finite linear combination of $T$ monomials, take the largest total loop degree $d$. The degree-$d$ homogeneous component is nonzero by step 1.2, even when degree-zero generators occur. Thus that combination belongs to $\bigoplus_{s\le d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$ and not to $\bigoplus_{s<d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$. Consequently the intersection filtration in the Statement is exactly the span of $T$ monomials of total loop degree at most $d$, and their degree-$d$ symbols form a basis of its associated graded. This verifies symbol independence directly, rather than inferring it from independence of filtered elements.

**The graded algebra isomorphism.** For any subalgebra of a nonnegatively graded algebra with its intersection filtration, taking highest homogeneous components embeds its associated graded into that graded algebra: if a representative's component of degree $d$ is zero it already lies in filtration $d-1$, and multiplication agrees with multiplication of homogeneous components. Apply this to $W(\lambda)\subseteq U(\mathfrak p)$. Step 2.1 identifies its image with the span of the ordered monomials in $\mathfrak g^e$, which is precisely the embedded algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ from step 1.2. Hence $\operatorname{gr}^{\mathrm{loop}}W(\lambda)\cong U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the identification sends the symbol of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$ as asserted.

**Filtration and the second graded algebra.** Each generator has finite nonnegative good degree, and each element is a finite sum of $T$ monomials, so the loop filtration is exhaustive and bounded below with $F_{-1}=0$. The actual homogeneous decomposition in $U(\mathfrak p)$ and step 2.1 give separatedness. The finite basis is already established in [F1], and step 3.1 establishes its filtered deformation property. Independently, the Kazhdan filtration uses positive weights $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)+1$ on $\mathfrak p$ and has associated graded $\mathbb C[S]$ by [F4]; in the doubled convention its weights are twice these. That graded algebra is commutative, whereas $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative whenever $\mathfrak g^e$ is nonabelian. These are the two claimed filtrations and their respective graded algebras.
