In the source convention $\lambda_i=a_i+i-1$, the coordinates $\lambda_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$ show that the central character is precisely this entry multiset. Hence the ground block has the sole column-strict label $A_c$. The generalized standard has diagonal simple multiplicity one and no other simple label in this block, so $N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Actual BGG reciprocity and the projective standard flag give $(P(A_c):N(A_c))=1$ and no other section, so $P_c=P(A_c)=N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Simple-preserving restricted duality makes this simple projective injective. The typed coset equivalence transports the same proof to every admissible complex origin. Tensoring has the exact ordinary-contragredient tensor adjoint on both sides, so $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is projective-injective. Simple-preserving restricted transposition duality fixes $P_c$ and the natural module and commutes with this tensor product; hence $T$ is self-dual. Its standard flag follows from the actual parabolic tensor identity, so step 2.4 gives a standard-label socle and duality gives a standard-label head. Conversely every degree-$d$ standard label $A$ is an incoming crystal move $\widetilde f_iB$ from a degree-$d-1$ standard label, except ground in degree zero. Inducting from the ground quotient, exact $f_i$ gives $f_iT_{d-1}\twoheadrightarrow f_iL_O(B)\twoheadrightarrow L_O(A)$ using the ACTUAL simple-head theorem; $f_iT_{d-1}$ is a summand of $T_d$, so $L_O(A)$ is a quotient of $T_d$. Lift any such quotient through its projective cover. Essentiality of the cover makes the lift $T_d\to P(A)$ surjective, and projectivity of $P(A)$ splits it. Therefore the projective summands of $T_d$ are exactly the covers of the standard-label simples, with positive multiplicities; they are injective as summands of $T_d$. It follows that every nonzero submodule $X\subseteq T_d$ has a nonzero standard-label simple socle. Exact $V$ and the nonvanishing already proved in step 1.18 then give $V(X)\ne0$. This proves the required detector; it does not assert that every composition factor of $T_d$ is standard or that $T_d$ generates the whole parabolic category.

For a finite-dimensional left $W$ module $M$, the left Whittaker lift of $m\otimes z_j$ is $\sum_i(X_{ij}\cdot1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes z_i$; the right lift of $f\otimes z^i$ is $\sum_j(f\otimes1_\chi\cdot Y_{ij})\otimes z^j$. The matrix equations put these vectors in the appropriate Whittaker spaces. Under the cofree constant-evaluation isomorphism from the proved Skryabin tensor construction, each lift is triangular in the finite column flag with diagonal identity; its off-diagonal entries are operators on M, so the finite nilpotent inverse proves it is an isomorphism. This constant evaluation is used only for invertibility, not identified with the balanced p-module tensor map. Set $A_Z(w)=Y_Z\delta_Z(w)X_Z$. Left Whittaker invariance makes its entries elements of the ORIGINAL $W$. The identity $\delta_Z(w)X_Z=X_ZA_Z(w)$ gives $w(m\otimes z_j)=\sum_iA_Z(w)_{ij}m\otimes z_i$; $Y_Z\delta_Z(w)=A_Z(w)Y_Z$ gives $(f\otimes z^i)w=\sum_jfA_Z(w)_{ij}\otimes z^j$. The head/tail shifts add Lie characters, so their coproduct identities reduce both computations to the same unshifted $\delta_Z$. Therefore the perfect finite pairing $\langle f\otimes\phi,m\otimes z\rangle=f(m)\phi(z)$ is a MODULE pairing: $(M\circledast Z)^*\cong M^*\circledast_{\mathrm{right}}Z^\vee$. This is the necessary algebra-action argument, rather than a vector-space duality substituted for it.

Fix an admissible origin: c_j−c_k integral implies c_j=c_k. The original arbitrary-origin deformed tensor algebra remains separate and unrestricted. In a column of height q whose global row numbers are n−q+1,…,n, write its strict entries a_1,…,a_q. The genuine head-model action proved in step 3.1 makes its finite-Levi highest weight nu_s=a_s+n−q+s−1. This follows directly from the global highest weight lambda_i=a_i+i−1 and eta_head diagonal shift n−q_1−…−q_col: the column-reading position i=q_before+(global_row−n+q) gives lambda_i+eta_head=a_i+global_row−1.

Apply the original-head right Skryabin counit $H_N\otimes_W Q_{\chi,\mathrm{right}}\to D_\chi N$, $f\otimes\overline a\mapsto fa$. Tensor it with $Z^\vee$, apply right Wh and use step 2.3 to obtain $H_N\circledast_{\mathrm{right}}Z^\vee\cong H_{N\otimes Z}$. Combine this actual counit with the module pairing of step 4.1 and take finite duals. This gives the natural $W$ isomorphism $\nu_{N,Z}:V(N\otimes Z)\to V(N)\circledast Z$ for EVERY genuine parabolic object $N$, including objects without an induced-module realization. Coassociativity, counit associativity and the inverse product formulas of step 3.2 make its two iterated tensor constructions agree under transported associativity. Naturality in a map of finite tensor factors follows from its ordinary dual map and the basis-independent evaluation pairing; hence adjacent flips are intertwined.

Compute the actual Casimir coefficients in ordinary box matrix units. On the LEFT lift, the coefficient at $v_k$ after $\Omega=\sum E_{ab}\otimes E_{ba}$ is $\sum_hE_{h,k}\eta_{\mathrm{tail}}X_{hj}$. Positive matrices give $(E_{h,k}-\delta_{hk}\rho_k^{\mathrm{tail}})X_{hj}$ after undoing the shift. Negative matrices give $\chi(E_{h,k})X_{hj}-X_{kj}$ by step 1.9. Their total scalar is $-\rho_k^{\mathrm{tail}}-\sum_{b>\operatorname{col}(k)}q_b=q_{\operatorname{col}(k)}-n$. On the RIGHT lift the coefficient at $v^h$ is $\sum_k\eta_{\mathrm{head}}Y_{ik}E_{h,k}$; step 2.2 moves negative matrices left, giving $\chi(E_{h,k})Y_{ik}-Y_{ih}$, and the total scalar is $-\rho_h^{\mathrm{head}}-\sum_{b<\operatorname{col}(h)}q_b=q_{\operatorname{col}(h)}-n$. Multiplying by $Y$ on the left or $X$ on the right therefore gives the SAME entries $C_{j,i}=\sum_{\operatorname{col}(h)\le\operatorname{col}(k)}Y_{i,k}E_{h,k}X_{h,j}+\sum_k(q_{\operatorname{col}(k)}-n)Y_{i,k}X_{k,j}+\sum_{\operatorname{row}(h)=\operatorname{row}(k),\,\operatorname{col}(h)=\operatorname{col}(k)-1}Y_{i,h}X_{k,j}$. There is no extra displacement sign on the ordinary $E_{h,k}$; signs are already in $X,Y$. The entries lie in $W$ because the Casimir preserves the actual Whittaker subspace. The module pairing now intertwines the two transported Casimirs, while the continuous tensor pairing transposes the source Casimir term by term. Hence $\nu$ intertwines the source and target Casimir maps. With flip compatibility this also intertwines their polynomial and generalized-eigenspace residue projections, with the usual contragredient retained for reverse translation.

Fix the head-normalized ground map $i_0:V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$ obtained from step 3.1 and the finite-Levi character calculation below. Iterate $\nu$ on $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes(d-1)}$ to obtain $i_d:V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\to\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}$, and compose with the proved ACTUAL balanced tensor map $\mu_d$ to get $j_d$. Casimir and flip compatibility prove $(W,H_d)$-bimodule linearity. Any source endomorphism $b$ is transported as $j_dV(b)j_d^{-1}$; in particular a native Casimir/place word representing right multiplication by $h$ becomes the actual map $m\mapsto mh$. This identifies maps in the cyclotomic IMAGE algebra, without asserting a faithful abstract Hecke action outside its allowed range. The construction uses no origin integrality. Typed category-O/coset transport is used only for the selected admissible-origin source labels and their character dictionaries, whereas the unrestricted deformed tensor model retains its arbitrary origins.

$H_d$ acts on $T$ by the universal tensor Casimir and places. At the first tensor step the actual finite $\mathfrak p$ flag of the natural module has one standard section per column. On the $j$th section, the ordinary quadratic-Casimir identity $\Omega=(C_{\mathrm{total}}-C_{\mathrm{source}}-C_V)/2$ gives eigenvalue $c_j+q_j-n$. Successively applying the factors in the column-order flag makes $\prod_j(x_1-(c_j+q_j-n))$ annihilate $T$; subsequent tensor factors leave this first-step relation intact. Hence the source action factors through the genuine cyclotomic algebra, not only its $V$ image. Step 7.1 transports it to $M=V_c^{\otimes d}$ as the actual $(W,H_d)$ bimodule action.

$V$ maps $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $\operatorname{End}_{W}(M)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$ by step 2.5, and its image contains $B$ because every target Hecke operator is the transport of its actual source Casimir/place operator. A nonzero source endomorphism has a nonzero image $X\subseteq T$. Step 3.3 proves $V(X)\ne0$, and exactness identifies $V(X)$ with the image of its transported endomorphism. Hence the endomorphism map is injective as well as surjective, giving $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$. Detection uses the standard-label SOCLE criterion, never a claim that all composition factors of $T$ are standard.

Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism.

A finite-dimensional right B-module whose tensor functor is exact is projective. Explicitly, take its finite projective cover P→M with kernel K⊂P rad B. Tensor the inclusion K→P with B/rad B; flatness makes K/K rad B inject into P/P rad B, but this map is zero, so Nakayama gives K=0. Faithfulness forces every right indecomposable projective to occur in M: otherwise tensor with the corresponding left simple would vanish. Thus M_B is a progenerator. The first independently proved raw centralizer identity in step 2.5 gives Wd=End_B(M). The usual generator presentation/evaluation argument now gives the genuine Morita equivalence Wd-mod≃B-mod. In particular F sends B-simples to Wd-simples, proving the full relevant V simple-image claim without assuming it earlier.

Tensor compatibility and the actual Casimir/flip intertwiners are proved in steps 1.9–1.18, using the original head/right normalizer and the actual balanced Skryabin map. Thus $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and $V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})=V_c^{\otimes d}$. The preceding kernel/Morita construction proves $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))=L_W(A)$ for standard labels and zero otherwise; it never asserts that the image of a source standard $N(A)$ is simple. The normalized comparison is determined on the ground and its tensor words, hence on the detecting tensor bimodule and on finite free quotient presentations through the established exact Morita factorization. Its ground normalization removes scalar ambiguity. This proves the stated properties of the genuine Whittaker functor, while keeping it distinct from the Hecke Hom quotient.

citations.quote:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration
$$F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$$
induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], and
likewise for the shifted Yangian of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
Then the associated graded algebra $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)$ is
canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as
a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading, and the
isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to
$(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, where the $e_{i,j;r}$ are the centralizer basis of the
pyramid. In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of
$U(\mathfrak g^e)$, the loop filtration is separated, and the ordered
monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of
$W(\lambda)$.

This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has
associated graded the commutative Slodowy-slice algebra $\mathbb C[S]$, while
here $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in
general.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

derivations.claim: The graded unital images. Write $E=V^{\otimes d}$, $C=W_d$, and $D$ for the right Hecke image viewed as an algebra of operators on $E$. The supplied actual tensor model in F1 gives commuting filtered operator algebras, with the graded symbols containing the unital images $A^0$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and $D^0$ of the truncated polynomial/permutation algebra. The character automorphism in F1 gives exactly the same $A^0$ as the untwisted representation; no equality of the fixed-chart twisted and untwisted modules is inferred. Since $A^0,D^0$ are mutual centralizers, taking leading homogeneous terms of commuting operators gives $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$, where $Z$ is the commutant in $\operatorname{End}(E)$. Interchanging $C,D$ gives $D^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}D\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(C)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}C)\subseteq Z(A^0)=D^0$. Thus every inclusion is equality, establishing strict equality of both graded images as well as their commutants.

The exact ordinary-dual adjoint. For a finite rational $\mathfrak g$-module $E$, Skryabin transports ordinary evaluation $E^*\otimes E\to\mathbb C$ and coevaluation $\mathbb C\to E\otimes E^*$ to the tensor functors $F_E(M)=M\circledast E$. The ordinary zigzag identities give both adjunctions between $F_E$ and $F_{E^*}$. These functors are exact: tensoring is exact, it preserves generalized Whittaker modules by a finite Engel-flag nilpotence bound, and Skryabin is an exact equivalence. They preserve $\mathcal R_c$: a faithful finite image module embeds the regular algebra into a finite direct sum of copies of itself by evaluation on a basis, so every finite-image module is a subquotient of a finite sum of tensor modules; exact tensor transport sends degree $d$ to degree $d+1$. For $N>0$, also $V^*=\bigwedge^{N-1}V\otimes\det^{-1}$, and the exterior power is a summand of a tensor power by the antisymmetrizer. Determinant shifts therefore give closure under $V^*$ too. Consequently $F_V$ preserves projectives in the entire rational category through its exact right adjoint $F_{V^*}$. Here $V^*$ is the ordinary contragredient natural module, distinct from $V$; the transpose contravariant duality of category $\mathcal O$ is not this adjoint.

The filtered centralizers. For an operator in $Z(D)$, equality of the induced graded spaces in step 1.1 supplies a member of $C$ with the same leading symbol. Subtracting lowers its integer filtration degree. The finite grading of $E$ bounds the induced endomorphism filtration below, so this terminates, proving $Z(D)=C$. The same procedure proves $Z(C)=D$. Returning to the right-action opposite convention gives both mutual-centralizer identities and the stated associated graded image algebras. At degree zero both images are scalar, while for an empty pyramid and positive degree $E=0$ and both are zero; these are already covered by the actual tensor model of F1. This proves clause (1) for every origin, without a Morita assumption.

Stable injectivity. For a nonempty pyramid with $q_l\ge d$, choose $d$ distinct terminal boxes on length-$l$ Jordan strings. In the associated graded tensor action each bounded PBW word $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, $0\le a_i<l$, sends their ordered terminal tensor to the tensor with those distinct strings permuted by $w$ and each box moved $a_i$ places left. These $l^dd!$ outputs are distinct basis tensors, so the graded PBW word images are independent. A nonzero filtered Hecke element has a nonzero leading PBW symbol, hence a nonzero leading operator and a nonzero actual operator. Thus the raw action is faithful. For the empty pyramid, degree zero is the scalar identity and positive-degree tensor space and cyclotomic algebra are zero, so the action is faithful there too without using an undefined $q_l$.

The finite-image row projectives. Assume $c$ admissible. A row occupancy $
u=(
u_1,\ldots,
u_n)$ determines a tuple $\mathbf j_
u$ of terminal row boxes and the diagonal row-multiset projection $e_
u$. Since the right tensor matrices preserve row multisets, $e_
u\in W_d$ by step 2.1; these orthogonal idempotents sum to one. Here is the actual basis of their projective left ideals. For a commuting matrix $\sum b_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}E_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$, place permutations identify diagonal $S_d$-orbits, and the $U(\mathfrak p)$ image forces $b_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}=0$ when some source column is smaller than its output column. Comparing its coefficients with $x_k$ and replacing $\mathbf j$ by $R_k(\mathbf j)$ expresses each nonterminal coefficient in coefficients with larger total source column sum: the first term is $b_{R_k(\mathbf i),R_k(\mathbf j)}$, the diagonal term is $(c_{\operatorname{col}(i_k)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(i_k)}-c_{\operatorname{col}(j_k)+1}-q_{\operatorname{col}(j_k)+1})b_{\mathbf i,R_k(\mathbf j)}$, and the two remaining sums run over swaps $(h\ k)$ with respectively both columns at most, or both columns greater than, the $k$th columns. Their signs are respectively plus and minus. This is terminating elimination from terminal source tuples. The graded string-orbit matrices are independent and indexed by the same terminal orbits, so step 1.1 makes the terminal-coordinate map an isomorphism. Let $\Xi_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j_
u}$ be the normalized preimages. Evaluation on $v_{\mathbf j_
u}$ gives exactly the orbit sums under $\prod_rS_{
u_r}$, which form the monomial basis of $Z_
u= igotimes_r\operatorname{Sym}^{
u_r}(V_{\le p_r})$ with its actual $c$-twist. Thus $W_de_
u\cong Z_
u$ as actual modules, and the regular module is their sum. This proves these projectivities in the finite image, without invoking Morita.

Projectivity of the ground object. For $r\ge0$, take degree $Nr$ and the one-dimensional determinant-shifted ground object $D_r=\mathbb C_c\circledast\det^r$, with tableau $A_{c+r\mathbf1}$. Its content reconstructs it uniquely among column-strict tableaux: in each charge coset the minimum appears in every column and hence in its bottom box; removing these boxes and repeating reconstructs all columns. Therefore its scalar central-character summand has exactly this one simple, by F3. The regular-module multiplicity of $D_r$ is one. Indeed, the Levi decomposition of $Z_\nu$ uses semistandard tableaux of shapes given by the column partitions of ground differences, with the alphabet in column $j$ consisting of the terminal row boxes whose rows reach that column. This follows by expanding the complete symmetric characters of its symmetric factors and using the Schur semistandard formula, or successive horizontal-strip multiplication; its finite radical filtration makes it an actual $\mathfrak p$-filtration by these Levi sections. For $D_r$ the shapes are rectangles $(r^{q_j})$ and the allowed alphabet has exactly $q_j$ letters. Each length-$q_j$ strictly increasing tableau column must contain every letter in order. There is exactly one tuple, and its row-$i$ multiplicity is $rp_i$. Thus the coefficient is one for $\nu_i=rp_i$ and zero for every other occupancy. Other standards cannot contain $D_r$ because their scalar central characters differ. The supported regular summand has length one and is $D_r$ itself, so $D_r$ is projective over $W_{Nr}$. For a surjection in the rational finite-W category $\mathcal R_c$, a common determinant twist puts its terms into finite sums of polynomial-image categories. The scalar degree operator splits these by degree. A map from $\mathbb C_c$ becomes a map from $D_r$ into the degree-$Nr$ summand, where it lifts by the projectivity just proved. The inverse determinant twist gives the original lift. Hence $\mathbb C_c$ is projective in $\mathcal R_c$, without claiming projectivity in arbitrary $W(\lambda)$-mod.

The finite-W projective covers. Put $Q(A)=\operatorname{Wh}(P(A))$ for standard labels. At degree zero this is the ground object, projective by step 4.1. For a positive-degree standard $A$, the actual standard-label crystal supplies $A=\widetilde f_iB$ and a quotient $L_O(B)\otimes V\to L_O(A)$. Lifting along the projective cover and splitting proves $P(A)$ is a summand of $P(B)\otimes V$. The genuine tensor comparison sends this to a summand of $Q(B)\circledast V$, projective by step 1.2. To identify its head, write $P(B)\otimes V=\bigoplus_C P(C)^{m_C}$ with standard $C$, using the independently proved detector head/socle property in F3. Exact Wh gives $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q(C),L_W(D))\ge\delta_{CD}$. On the other hand ordinary-dual adjunction, the induction hypothesis and the genuine simple/tensor comparison give $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q(B)\circledast V,L_W(D))=[L_W(D)\circledast V^*:L_W(B)]=[L_O(D)\otimes V^*:L_O(B)]=m_D$. Comparing this equality with the sum over $C$ forces $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q(C),L_W(D))=\delta_{CD}$ for every summand with $m_C>0$. Thus each $Q(A)$ is the genuine projective cover of $L_W(A)$. Exhaustion of finite-image simples and occurrence of every standard cover in the detecting tensor object now show that $U_d=\operatorname{Wh}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod. This uses the actual simple-image and tensor maps of F3, rather than inferring covers from characters or mutual centralizers.

Morita for the finite images. Since $U_d$ is a finite projective generator of $W_d$-mod, every module admits a presentation by finite sums of $U_d$. The evaluation maps from the tensor-Hom adjunction are isomorphisms on $U_d$ and its direct sums and summands, hence on every module by passing to the cokernels of such presentations. Conversely the same argument for presentations of modules over $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(U_d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives the inverse evaluation. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U_d,-)$ is an equivalence with inverse $U_d\otimes_{B_d}-$, and step 2.1 identifies its target algebra with the genuine Hecke image $B_d$. This proves clause (3) under admissibility independently of any supporting-block Morita assumption. In the empty-pyramid case the positive-degree tensor and both image algebras are zero, so their module categories are zero and the equivalence is immediate; degree zero is the scalar equivalence.

The nonadmissible boundary. For $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$, the explicit finite matrix computed from the tensor action shows that the tensor module is not projective over $B_d$, so the progenerator hypothesis fails; the mutual centralizers of step 2.1 still hold. This is the companion-page example separating the two assertions.
