citations.quote:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i,i+1}$), and
$F_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i+1,i}$). For $i<j$, the higher-root
coefficients $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{i,j}$ and
$F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{j,i}$; they are defined recursively by
adjacent-root commutators, not declared as a duplicate independent family.
These generators are subject to the shifted Drinfeld relations of the source (the
shifted analogues of the $D$-$D$, $D$-$E$, $D$-$F$, $E$-$E$, $F$-$F$ and
$E$-$F$ relations, with the shift matrix $\sigma$ entering through the ranges
and the constants). Two filtrations are fixed on it: the **canonical
filtration**, in which each generator of upper index $r$ has degree $r$, and
the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra and $M$ a finite-dimensional left
$A$-module. Then $M$ has a projective cover. If $\pi:P\to M$ and $\rho:Q\to M$
are projective covers, then there is an isomorphism $f:P\to Q$ with
$\rho\circ f=\pi$.

Let $A=k[G]$ with $k$ a splitting field for the finite group $G$. Then the
left regular module decomposes as

$$ {}_A A\cong\bigoplus_{S\in\operatorname{Irr}(A)} P(S)^{\oplus \dim_k S}, $$

where $P(S)$ is the projective cover of the simple module $S$.

derivations.claim: The retained projection is an actual left-image idempotent. The matrix $e=\sum_{\mathbf i\in I^d}E_{\hat{\mathbf i},\hat{\mathbf i}}$ commutes with the right $x_k$ and $s_k$: left-neighbour moves, place swaps and scalar terms preserve the row multiset, so none changes zero deleted-row occupancy. Thus $e\in A_d^{\mathrm{big}}$ by the independent first centralizer. Every term of the right tensor formula restricts identically under $v_{\mathbf i}\mapsto v_{\hat{\mathbf i}}$, because row and column positions and left neighbours agree and $c_j+(q_j+t)-(n+t)=a_j$. This proves the actual right-bimodule identification $eU^{\mathrm{big}}=U$ and a surjective restriction map $\rho:B_d^{\mathrm{big}}\to B_d$. Extending a commuting operator on $eU^{\mathrm{big}}$ by zero on $(1-e)U^{\mathrm{big}}$ shows $A_d=eA_d^{\mathrm{big}}e$. No Morita conclusion is used.

The standard contraction has the same corner action. In column $j$ the finite Levi module is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j+t})$, with $\mu^{(j)}$ the partition of the ground differences. The zero-occupancy part is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j})$, by the tensor Young-symmetrizer realization; it is zero precisely when a removed-row partition entry is nonzero. For the original $T_{ij;0}^{(r)}$ path sum, every summand is a product of matrix units with strictly increasing join columns. Levi projection kills strict off-column matrix factors, leaving at most one factor in each column. A deleted intermediate row causes an off-diagonal crossing in a column whose removed-coordinate occupancy then cannot be restored by another factor, so zero-occupancy compression kills it. Every surviving path has only retained rows and is exactly a small path. The head shift changes by $-(j-1)t$ in column $j$, while a retained box's ordinary source reading position changes by $+(j-1)t$. Its source highest weight $A_{\mathrm{box}}+k-1$ therefore cancels that shift: the normalized weight is $A_{\mathrm{box}}+\operatorname{row}(\mathrm{box})-1$ in both diagrams. Hence the complete retained matrix action, and then formal Gauss elimination, gives $eV(A)=V(\bar A)$ for contractible $A$, and zero otherwise, with the corner identification of step 1.1.

The simple contraction and central saturation. The same projector acts on all standards: let $H_r=T_{rr;0}^{(1)}$ be the row Cartan and $\kappa_r=\sum_{j:\text{row }r\text{ reaches column }j}c_j$. Its head-normalized action on a degree-$d$ Levi standard has $H_r-\kappa_r$ equal to polynomial row occupancy with eigenvalues $0,\ldots,d$. Hence $e=\prod_{r\text{ deleted}}\prod_{h=1}^d(1-(H_r-\kappa_r)/h)$ is exactly zero removed-row occupancy on every standard and equals step 1.1's image idempotent; for $d=0$ the inner product is one. Exactness of $e(-)$ and step 2.1 therefore kill every noncontractible simple. For a surviving big simple $L$, each nonzero $v\in eL$ generates $eL=eA_d^{\mathrm{big}}ev$, so $eL$ is simple. Conversely for a corner simple $S$, every proper submodule of $A_d^{\mathrm{big}}e\otimes_{eA_d^{\mathrm{big}}e}S$ is killed by $e$: one with image $S$ generates that whole induced module. The sum of proper submodules is thus proper and is its unique maximal submodule. Its simple quotient has $e$-image $S$. This proves a bijection between corner simples and surviving big simples without a Morita assumption. Every small standard tableau extends uniquely by full ground rows to a contractible large standard tableau. The complete Std simple lists in F2 and the corner of step 1.1 show that the survivor subset has the same finite cardinality as all contractible Std labels, so every contractible simple survives. Its simple image is a quotient of $eV(A)=V(\bar A)$, whose already proved unique head gives $eL_W(A)=L_W(\bar A)$. If $\theta(B)=\theta(A)$ and $A$ is contractible, separate the charge cosets. Admissibility makes all charges in one coset equal. The minimal bottom entry $c_j+1-(n+t)$ occurs once in every column of that coset; strictness and nonnegative ground differences force these occurrences into the same bottom row of $B$. Remove that row and repeat for all deleted rows. Then $B$ is contractible. Scalar central characters therefore separate contractible from noncontractible simples, so generalized central-character decomposition gives a central idempotent $f\in A_d^{\mathrm{big}}$ with exactly that support. Since $e$ kills all complementary simples, $e(1-f)=0$: a nonzero idempotent acts nontrivially on some simple of a finite algebra. Hence $e=ef=fe$.

Fullness and the supported module equivalence. Set $A_f=fA_d^{\mathrm{big}}f$. Every simple $A_f$-module survives $e$. If $A_feA_f$ were proper, the nonzero finite quotient $A_f/A_feA_f$ would have a simple killed by $e$, a contradiction. Thus write $f=\sum_k a_keb_k$. Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

derivations.claim: **The tower map and both finite free structures.** The first $d$ dot and crossing generators in $A$ satisfy the relations of $B$, including the same cyclotomic polynomial in $x_1$. Their bounded PBW words are a subset of the bounded basis of $A$, so the generator-preserving homomorphism is injective. Let $w_t=s_t\cdots s_d$ for $1\le t\le d$ and $w_{d+1}=1$; these are the minimal right $S_d$ coset representatives in $S_{d+1}$, with $w_t(d+1)=t$. The elements $w_tx_{d+1}^r$, $0\le r<l$, form a right $B$-basis of $A$. Indeed multiply them by the bounded PBW basis of $B$. In the associated graded algebra their symbols are the distinct bounded words obtained by permuting the first $d$ dot exponents by $w_t$ and placing exponent $r$ in the omitted position $t$, with permutation $w_tv$, $v\in S_d$. These run over exactly all bounded words of $\operatorname{gr}A$, so filtered leading-degree induction proves that the products form a basis of $A$. Applying $*$ gives the left $B$-basis $\eta_{t,r}=x_{d+1}^rw_t^{-1}$. Thus both ranks are $l(d+1)$, and this is valid without any separation of roots.

**An actual relative Frobenius trace.** Use the two symmetric traces to define $t:A\to B$ uniquely by $\tau_d(bt(a))=\tau_{d+1}(ba)$ for every $b\in B$. Nondegeneracy of $\tau_d$ proves existence and uniqueness. Cyclicity of both traces gives $t(b_1ab_2)=b_1t(a)b_2$, so $t$ is a $B$-bimodule map. The map $\Phi:A\to\operatorname{Hom}_B({}_BA,{}_BB)$, $\Phi(a)(c)=t(ca)$, is an $(A,B)$-bimodule isomorphism, where the left action on Hom is $(a\cdot h)(c)=h(ca)$ and its right action is multiplication on the output. To see invertibility directly, $h\mapsto\tau_d\circ h$ identifies this Hom space with $D_{\mathbb C}A$: given $\lambda\in D_{\mathbb C}A$, define $h(c)$ by $\tau_d(bh(c))=\lambda(bc)$, which is uniquely determined and $B$-linear. The symmetric $A$-trace identifies $A$ with $D_{\mathbb C}A$ by $a\mapsto[c\mapsto\tau_{d+1}(ca)]$. Their composite is precisely $\Phi$, including both bimodule actions. This proves the Frobenius extension identity using the two traces and the actual finite extension, rather than assuming tensor products commute with linear duality.

**The projectors and residue chains.** For each regular-spectrum eigenvalue $i$ of $x_{d+1}$, apply [F2] to its annihilating polynomial to obtain $u_i\in\mathbb C[x_{d+1}]$. Since the regular representation is faithful and every finite module is a quotient of a finite free module, these projectors act as the generalized-eigenspace projectors on every module. Cross relations show $x_{d+1}$ commutes with $B$, so $u_i$ centralizes $B$ and is fixed by $*$. Their products and sum give the stated orthogonality and identity. For the root-coset claim use joint dot projectors and $\phi_r=s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})+1$, which satisfies $\phi_r^2=1-(x_r-x_{r+1})^2$ and swaps the adjacent dot operators. On a weight with adjacent entries differing by neither $1$ nor $-1$, this square is invertible by a finite nilpotent geometric series. A leftmost eigenvalue outside $\bigcup_j(a_j+\mathbb Z)$ can therefore be moved past all preceding entries in that union, since its differences from them are not integers; this produces a nonzero first-position eigenvalue contradicting the cyclotomic relation. Thus every eigenvalue lies on one of the specified coset chains. No orbit-sum primitivity is used.

**Induction equals coinduction, with explicit inverse.** Index the left basis $\eta_s$ from step 1.1 by $s=(t,r)$ and let $p_s:A\to B$ be its left-coordinate maps, so $c=\sum_sp_s(c)\eta_s$. Put $a_s=\Phi^{-1}p_s$. Then $t(\eta_sa_{s'})=\delta_{ss'}$ and $c=\sum_st(ca_s)\eta_s$. Finite freeness makes the natural map $\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,B)\otimes_BN\to\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,N)$ an isomorphism: it sends $h\otimes n$ to $[c\mapsto h(c)n]$ and its inverse sends $g$ to $\sum_sp_s\otimes g(\eta_s)$. Composing with $\Phi$ gives the natural $A$-module isomorphism $A\otimes_BN\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B({}_BA,N)$, $a\otimes n\mapsto[c\mapsto t(ca)n]$, with inverse $g\mapsto\sum_sa_s\otimes g(\eta_s)$. Consequently induction is both left and right adjoint to ordinary restriction. It is exact by the right freeness in step 1.1, independently of any duality argument.

**The residue Frobenius isomorphism and two adjunctions.** Write $u=u_i$. For every $c\in A$, one has $t(uc)=t(cu)$: pairing either side with $b\in B$ under $\tau_d$ gives $\tau_{d+1}(buc)=\tau_{d+1}(bcu)$ by $bu=ub$ and trace cyclicity. Hence right multiplication by $u$ on $A$ corresponds under $\Phi$ to precomposition by left multiplication by $u$. Restricting the isomorphism of step 3.1 therefore gives $Au\otimes_BN\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B({}_BuA,N)$ as left $A$-modules, with the same explicit relative-trace formula on $uA$. The usual tensor-Hom adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_A(Au\otimes_BN,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,uM)$, and the usual restriction-coinduction adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_B(uM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\operatorname{Hom}_B(uA,N))$. Together these prove $f_i\dashv e_i\dashv f_i$. The functor $e_i$ is exact as an idempotent summand of restriction; $Au$ is a right-$B$ direct summand of the free module $A$, so $f_i$ is exact. The units and counits are the tensor-Hom evaluation maps and the relative-trace/dual-basis coinduction maps just constructed, not maps inferred from an abstract symmetry of two algebras.

**The correct dual tensor comparison.** For a left $A$-module $X$ write $D_AX=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(X,\mathbb C)$ with action twisted by $*$, and write $D_BN$ for the same construction on the left $B$-module $N$. The actual natural isomorphism is $D_A(A\otimes_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B({}_BA,D_BN)$. It sends a linear functional $\lambda$ to $[c\mapsto(n\mapsto\lambda(c^*\otimes n))]$, with inverse $h\mapsto[a\otimes n\mapsto h(a^*)(n)]$. The balancing relation and $*$ show $B$-linearity and $A$-linearity directly. Composing its inverse with the genuine induction/coinduction isomorphism of step 3.1 gives $A\otimes_BD_BN\cong D_A(A\otimes_BN)$. The same formulas for the summands give $D_A(Au\otimes_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(uA,D_BN)\cong Au\otimes_BD_BN$, since $u^*=u$ and step 4.1 applies. Restriction similarly gives $uD_AM\cong D_B(uM)$ by restricting functionals, with inverse extending by zero on $(1-u)M$. Thus each residue functor commutes with ordinary $*$-duality. This proof does not identify $Au$ with its linear dual as an unqualified bimodule.

**Projectives and Grothendieck operators.** Exact biadjunction proves projective preservation: for projective $P$, $\operatorname{Hom}_A(f_iP,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(P,e_i-)$ is exact, and $\operatorname{Hom}_B(e_iQ,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,f_i-)$ is exact for projective $Q$. The Hom pairing descends to split $K_0$ of projectives and $G_0$ of finite-dimensional modules, because Hom is additive on projective direct sums and exact in its second variable. The two adjunctions compute $\langle[f_iP],[M]\rangle=\langle[P],[e_iM]\rangle$ and $\langle[e_iQ],[N]\rangle=\langle[Q],[f_iN]\rangle$. Exactness makes all operators well defined on these groups. Central source/target projections restrict the bimodules, adjunctions and duality comparisons to supported content summands; no primitivity premise is required for those restrictions.

**Boundaries and level zero.** The entire proof used only the actual bounded PBW extension and its two symmetric traces, so it applies to all complex roots and their repetitions. The realization assertion invokes only the actual admissible projected tensor actions of the named stable-range supplier, not a block-primitivity assertion. For $l=0$ the empty cyclotomic polynomial is $1$, so every positive-degree algebra is zero; the map $\mathbb C\to0$ is explicitly noninjective, all positive-degree functors are zero, and their exactness and adjunctions are the unique zero-functor ones. Together with steps 1.1–5.1 this proves every asserted boundary and functor property.

Work over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]],
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Fix $N\ge1$, let
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its matrix units $E_{ij}$ and the
trace form $B(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, which is symmetric, nondegenerate and
invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]), and let
$$z:=\sum_{i=1}^NE_{ii}\in\mathfrak g$$
be the central element (the identity matrix). The dual basis of $(E_{ij})$
under $B$ is $(E_{ji})$, so the Casimir element of
[[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]] is
$$\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^NE_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g),$$
and its operator on every $\mathfrak g$-module is the image under the
representation, commuting with the $\mathfrak g$-action
([[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]],
[[lem-the-casimir-element-is-independent-of-dual-bases]]).

Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak g$-module and $V=\mathbb C^N$ the natural module
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). On the tensor product
$M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]],
[[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) label the factors
$0,1,\dots,d$, with factor $0$ equal to $M$. For $0\le a\ne b\le d$ let
$\Omega_{ab}$ denote the operator obtained by applying $\Omega$ in the two
labelled factors, and for distinct $0\le a,b\le d$ let $P_{ab}$ denote the
operator that interchanges the two labelled factors (the flip of
$V\otimes V$ on two $V$-factors). Define, for $1\le j\le d$ and
$1\le i\le d-1$,
$$x_j:=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj},\qquad s_i:=P_{i,i+1}.$$
Finally put $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}:=\Omega-\tfrac1Nz\otimes z$ and define the
Arakawa-Suzuki normalized operators
$$y_j:=x_j-\tfrac1Nz_M+\tfrac{N-1}{2},$$
where $z_M$ denotes the endomorphism of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ given by the
action of $z$ on the factor $M$ (so $z_M$ acts as the representation of the
central element $z$ of $\mathfrak g$).

The verification below records the properties of these operators used on this
page: $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; the operators $x_j$ and
$s_i$ are natural in $M$ and commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action; the
recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ holds; $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}$ is the Casimir
of $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ relative to the restricted trace form; and the operators
$y_j$ are exactly the source operators of [AS, (2.2.2)]. For $d=0$ the family
$(x_j)$ is empty; for the trivial module $M=\mathbb C$ one has $\Omega_{0j}=0$,
so $x_j=\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $x_1=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Keep a nonempty pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with $l=p_n>0$ columns of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, the origin $c$, and $U_d=V_c^{\otimes d}$ of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable range** is $q_l\ge d$: there are at least $d$ rows of maximum length $l$. Put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, $A_d=\operatorname{im}(W(\lambda)\to\operatorname{End}U_d)$ and $B_d=\operatorname{im}(H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}U_d^{\mathrm{op}})$.

For every complex origin the finite image algebras are mutual centralizers, and the raw Hecke action is faithful in the stable range. For an **admissible** origin, meaning $c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_j=c_k$, the following construction defines the central support outside that range. Append $t$ full ground rows of length $l$ until $q_l+t\ge d$, keeping $l$ and $c$ fixed. Then $n$ and every $q_j$ increase by $t$, so every $a_j$ stays fixed. In the enlarged tensor space $U_d^{\mathrm{big}}$, let $e$ be the projection onto tensors using only retained rows, equivalently having zero occupancy in every deleted row. A large tableau is **contractible** if every deleted-row entry is the ground entry $c_j+1-r$ in row $r$ and column $j$. The supporting central idempotent $f$ acts as one on precisely the contractible standard-labelled simples and as zero on the others. Through the faithful enlarged Hecke action it is a central idempotent of $H_d(\mathbf a)$, and
$$B_d\cong fH_d(\mathbf a)f,\qquad\ker\psi_d=(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a).$$

This $f$ is a sum of entire supporting central blocks. Individual residue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ need not be central; they do not individually define this two-sided corner. The unrestricted tensor model does not by itself supply the admissible central-support conclusion.

For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the convention is separate: in degree zero the tensor and image algebras are $\mathbb C$ with the identity corner $f=1$; in positive degree the tensor, image algebras and their module categories are zero and $f=0$. No $q_l$ or nonempty stable-range condition is used in that case.

derivations.claim: The Hecke action lies in the g-endomorphisms. For the empty pyramid, the empty tensor in degree zero and its ground object give $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$. In positive degree $V=0$ gives $T_d=U_d=0$, and the level-zero cyclotomic relation is the empty product $1$, so $H_d=0$. The stated endomorphism identities and faithfulness follow directly, with the unique zero-algebra map injective; the remaining argument assumes a nonempty pyramid. Each generator $x_j$ of the truncated tensor action is built from the trace Casimir and place permutations and commutes with the diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action; the place permutations are natural in the module variable, so the resulting right $H_d(\mathbf a)$-action on $T$ consists of $\mathfrak g$-endomorphisms, and its image is $B_d$ by definition. Hence there is a surjection $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ and an inclusion $B_d\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the opposite convention fixed by the right action.

The Whittaker comparison is injective. Let $\varphi:T\to T$ be nonzero and put $X=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, a nonzero submodule of the finite-length object $T$. Choose a simple submodule $L(A)\subseteq X$; because $\operatorname{soc}X\subseteq\operatorname{soc}T$, [F2] gives $A\in\mathrm{Std}$. Exactness gives an injection $V(L(A))\hookrightarrow V(X)$, and the first module is nonzero, so $V(X)\ne0$. Exactness also identifies $V(X)$ with the image of $V(\varphi)$, hence $V(\varphi)\ne0$. This proves injectivity of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. No restriction on all composition factors of $T$ is used.

The image of the comparison. On $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$ the induced map lands in the centralizer of the finite-W action, $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$; by the filtered double centralizer [F3] this centralizer equals $B_d$; and the induced map contains $B_d$ because every Hecke generator on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ arises from the corresponding endomorphism of $T$ by [F1]. Since $B_d$ is the whole target, the injective map of step 1.2 is also surjective, so $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$.

Stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ then the action of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful by [F3] and the image is the full algebra $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$; a single central component is correspondingly a block $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$, not the whole algebra. Outside the stable range the corner identification of [F4] applies for admissible origins, while the map $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ remains surjective by step 1.1.

Central components. The central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of the finite-dimensional algebra $B_d$ decompose $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$ and $B_d=\bigoplus_\alpha B_\alpha$; applying the isomorphism of step 2.1 componentwise gives $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=f_\alpha B_df_\alpha=B_\alpha$. The component $B_\alpha$ sits inside the cyclotomic block as the corner $f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha$ by [F4]; it is not the entire degree-$d$ algebra.

Failure of raw faithfulness below the stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, suppose $d>q_l$ and use an enlargement by full ground rows with smallest height at least $d$. In its last column, raise the first $q_l+1$ entries above their ground values by $1$; raise its top entry further by $d-q_l-1$, and leave every other entry ground. This is column strict, has total degree $d$, and is standard: for columns with the same charge, the changed rightmost entry is at least every unchanged entry to its left in that row; different charge cosets are incomparable. The first $q_l$ rows of this column are retained, but its next row is deleted, so this standard label is noncontractible. Its nonzero large finite-W simple belongs to a complementary central block. Hence the supporting idempotent $f$ of [F4] is proper; the faithful large tensor progenerator makes $1-f$ nonzero also in the large Hecke algebra. The small raw action has the nonzero kernel $(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a)$ and is not faithful. Together with step 2.2 this proves the asserted precise stable-range criterion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns

[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$

algebra. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely when $q_l\ge d$ for a nonempty pyramid. For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the degree-zero objects and algebras are $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$, and for $d>0$ they are $T_d=U_d=H_d=0$. central decomposition. For a charge $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$

let $T_\alpha$ be the corresponding central component of $T$; in the integral
model
$$T_\alpha=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c,$$

$$B_\alpha:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}},$$

convention is fixed here), and define the **Schur functor** of the block by
$$\pi_\alpha:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha,-)\colon\mathcal O_\alpha^d\to B_\alpha\text{-mod}.$$
Its left adjoint is $\pi^*_\alpha:=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}-$.

standard-filtered quotient. Exact projection gives $G_\alpha$ on the entire
central block. The tensor detector $T_\alpha$ remains the object defining
$\pi_\alpha$; $G_\alpha$ generates all Col labels, while $T_\alpha$ contains
the standard-labelled projective-injective covers. These roles are distinct.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

derivations.claim: The raw double centralizer. For arbitrary complex origin the filtered leading-symbol lifting argument of [F1] gives $W_d=B_d'$ and $B_d=W_d'$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, with associated graded images the Vust centralizers; this is the all-origin clause and does not use admissibility.

below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

Keep the pyramid and admissible origins $c$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], the
ground object $P_c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and its
central decomposition. For a charge $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$
let $I_\alpha$ be the finite set of residue sequences of content $\alpha$, and
let $T_\alpha$ be the corresponding central component of $T$; in the integral
model
$$T_\alpha=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c,$$
the sum of the residue-induction images of the ground object. Put
$$B_\alpha:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the corresponding central component of the Hecke image algebra (the opposite
convention is fixed here), and define the **Schur functor** of the block by
$$\pi_\alpha:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha,-)\colon\mathcal O_\alpha^d\to B_\alpha\text{-mod}.$$
Its left adjoint is $\pi^*_\alpha:=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}-$.

For the whole polynomial $\mathrm{Col}_c^d$ summand, use the distinct finite projective generator
$$G_d=\bigoplus_{A\in\mathrm{Tab}^d}Z(A,c),$$
with actual prefix symmetric modules $Z(A,c)$ as constructed independently from the raw inducing modules in steps 1.2, 2.2, 3.2 and 4.1 of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]. Every category-O
projective cover is a summand of $G_d$; every $Z(A,c)$ embeds in $T_d$ with a
standard-filtered quotient. Exact projection gives $G_\alpha$ on the entire
central block. The tensor detector $T_\alpha$ remains the object defining
$\pi_\alpha$; $G_\alpha$ generates all Col labels, while $T_\alpha$ contains
the standard-labelled projective-injective covers. These roles are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page and marks the
boundaries explicitly: $\pi_\alpha$ is exact, being Hom from a projective
object; its left adjoint is right exact but not exact in general; it sends
$B_\alpha$-projectives to projective objects and $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha$
recovers $\operatorname{add}(T_\alpha)$, including every standard-labelled
prinjective; neither exactness of $\pi^*_\alpha$ nor recovery of every
category-$\mathcal O$ projective is asserted, both failing in the two-equal-charge
rank-one example of the companion page. The components assemble as a locally
unital sum over the charges, and all ambient labels, including those killed by
$\pi$, remain in the category $\mathcal O$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective.
4. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c$ be an admissible origin, let $P_c$ be the ground
simple projective-injective of the relevant summand of the parabolic category
$\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and let $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with $V=\mathbb C^N$. Write
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ for the image of the right cyclotomic Hecke action of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$
and on each central component, cut by the central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of
$B_d$ acting on $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$
where $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$ is the corresponding block of the cyclotomic Hecke
algebra. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely when $q_l\ge d$ for a nonempty pyramid. For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the degree-zero objects and algebras are $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$, and for $d>0$ they are $T_d=U_d=H_d=0$. All endomorphism identities hold there, and the raw action is faithful in every degree, including the zero-algebra action; $q_l$ is not defined in this branch.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Keep a nonempty pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with $l=p_n>0$ columns of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, the origin $c$, and $U_d=V_c^{\otimes d}$ of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable range** is $q_l\ge d$: there are at least $d$ rows of maximum length $l$. Put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, $A_d=\operatorname{im}(W(\lambda)\to\operatorname{End}U_d)$ and $B_d=\operatorname{im}(H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}U_d^{\mathrm{op}})$.

For every complex origin the finite image algebras are mutual centralizers, and the raw Hecke action is faithful in the stable range. For an **admissible** origin, meaning $c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_j=c_k$, the following construction defines the central support outside that range. Append $t$ full ground rows of length $l$ until $q_l+t\ge d$, keeping $l$ and $c$ fixed. Then $n$ and every $q_j$ increase by $t$, so every $a_j$ stays fixed. In the enlarged tensor space $U_d^{\mathrm{big}}$, let $e$ be the projection onto tensors using only retained rows, equivalently having zero occupancy in every deleted row. A large tableau is **contractible** if every deleted-row entry is the ground entry $c_j+1-r$ in row $r$ and column $j$. The supporting central idempotent $f$ acts as one on precisely the contractible standard-labelled simples and as zero on the others. Through the faithful enlarged Hecke action it is a central idempotent of $H_d(\mathbf a)$, and
$$B_d\cong fH_d(\mathbf a)f,\qquad\ker\psi_d=(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a).$$

This $f$ is a sum of entire supporting central blocks. Individual residue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ need not be central; they do not individually define this two-sided corner. The unrestricted tensor model does not by itself supply the admissible central-support conclusion.

For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the convention is separate: in degree zero the tensor and image algebras are $\mathbb C$ with the identity corner $f=1$; in positive degree the tensor, image algebras and their module categories are zero and $f=0$. No $q_l$ or nonempty stable-range condition is used in that case.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the genuine tableau
$K_0$/Fock identification at $s=1$
([[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]). For
every label $A$,
$$[L(A)]=L_A,\qquad [P(A)]=P_A,\qquad [T(A)]=T_A .$$
The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG reciprocity; the tilting
coefficients are the **opposite/reverse-column** composition coefficients
$\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not
generally the inverse-transpose of the original composition matrix. Simples,
projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and
canonical Fock families respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no
Koszul grading and no identification of the library upper and lower families is
asserted.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

derivations.claim: **A regular corner in the stable realization.** Add full ground rows until there are $d$ distinct rows of length $l$, and choose one rightmost box in each such row; let $v_S$ be their ordered tensor and $e_S$ the row-weight projection onto tensors using these rows once each. The actual tensor matrices in [F3] preserve row multisets, so this projection commutes with the right Hecke action and belongs to the left image by the first centralizer. The vectors $v_Sx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$, $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$, have distinct leading tensors: the leading dot moves its box one column left, while a permutation changes the ordered distinct rows. They therefore form a basis of $e_SU$ by triangularity, and its cardinality is $l^dd!$. Thus $b\mapsto v_Sb$ identifies $e_SU$ with the right regular $H_d(\mathbf a)$-module. Put $A=\operatorname{End}_{H_d(\mathbf a)}U$. Since $e_SU$ is regular, $Ae_S=\operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(e_SU,U)\cong U$ by evaluation at $v_S$. Consequently $h:H_d(\mathbf a)\to e_SAe_S$, characterized by $h(b)v_S=v_Sb$, is an algebra isomorphism, and $\theta\mapsto\theta(v_S)$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(U,M)$ with $e_SM$ for every finite-image module $M$. The left Hecke action on this corner is $h$, not the naive right action on $M$.

**The cyclic symmetric generator and its bottom quotient.** Write $A-A_c=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ and form the actual cumulative-column $\mathfrak p$-module $Z=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V_{\le\operatorname{col}(i)})$. Its bottom column degree is $b=\sum_i a_i(l-\operatorname{col}(i))$; the higher-degree part is a $\mathfrak p$-submodule, and $Z/Z_{>b}$ is the inflated Levi module $Z_b=\bigotimes_j\bigotimes_r\operatorname{Sym}^{\mu_r^{(j)}}(E_j)$. Put $w_A=\sum_{w\in\prod_iS_{a_i}}w$ and $x_A=\prod_i\prod_{k=1}^{a_i}\prod_{j>\operatorname{col}(i)}(x_{a_1+\cdots+a_{i-1}+k}-a_j)$. Apply these factors in order starting with the first tensor place. The actual dot formula gives $v_Sx_A=v_{\mathbf j}$, where $\mathbf j$ has the ordered rows of $v_S$ and column sequence prescribed by $A-A_c$; subtracting $a_j$ cancels the scalar at column $j$ and moves that box one column left. Hence $v_Sx_Aw_A=v_{\mathbf j}w_A\in e_SZ$. More generally the vectors $v_Swx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}x_Aw_A$, with $0\le r_k<\operatorname{col}(\mathbf j_k)$ and $w$ ranging over cosets of $\prod_i S_{a_i}$, have distinct leading symmetrized tensors and span $e_SZ$ by the ordinary symmetric-tensor basis. Thus this vector generates $e_SZ$ as a corner module, and its image generates $e_S(Z/Z_{>b})$. These are actual vector identities and triangular basis statements, rather than a character identification.

**The affine colour fibre.** Ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak h}(U,Z_b)\cong\bigotimes_j M^{\mu^{(j)}}$ on the canonical colour fibre, where $M^{\mu}$ is the symmetric-group permutation module. Its vectors in the corner are $v_{\mathbf j}ww_A+e_SZ_{>b}$ with $w\in S_{d_1}\times\cdots\times S_{d_l}$. For $k=d_1+\cdots+d_{j-1}+1$, the identity $v_{\mathbf j}=v_Sx_A$ and commutativity of dots give $h(x_k)v_{\mathbf j}ww_A=v_Sx_Ax_kww_A=v_{\mathbf j}x_kww_A$. In the bottom quotient the dot formula has scalar $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$: its left-neighbour term has higher degree, all preceding places have strictly smaller column and all later places have greater or equal column, so both signed transposition sums are empty. Thus $x_k$ acts as $a_j$ on that canonical fibre. The affine cross relations then determine the remaining dots as $a_j$ plus their within-block Jucys-Murphy sums. This proves that the fibre inclusion is a homomorphism for the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{d_l}$, with module $\bigotimes_j\mathrm{ev}_{a_j}^*M^{\mu^{(j)}}$, and its image generates the entire corner by step 2.1.

**The genuine Specht isomorphism.** The Levi Young-symmetrizer map gives an actual quotient $Z_b\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$ and hence a $\mathfrak p$-quotient $Z/Z_{>b}\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$. The canonical colour fibre quotient is $\bigotimes_j S^{\mu^{(j)}}$, by ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl. The affine fibre map in step 3.1 descends through this actual quotient and still generates: $e_S$ is exact and the generating vector of its source maps onto a generator of its quotient. Affine induction therefore gives a surjection $S(A)\twoheadrightarrow e_SV(A)$. The multilinear row-weight part of $\bigotimes_j S_{\mu^{(j)}}(E_j)$ has one summand for each allocation of the $d$ distinct rows into ordered colour subsets of sizes $d_j$, and on each subset its weight space is the polytabloid Specht space. Its dimension is $d!/(d_1!\cdots d_l!)\prod_j\dim S^{\mu^{(j)}}$. This is also the induced module's dimension, since the affine algebra is free over its affine Young subalgebra with the finite shuffle basis. The existing surjection is therefore an isomorphism. Steps 1.1 and [F2] identify its target with $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))=\pi(N(A))$, preserving the actual Hecke maps.

**Descent to the original pyramid.** Extend the original label $A$ by the added ground rows, producing a contractible large label $A^+$. Its column partitions $\mu^{(j)}$ and roots $a_j$ are unchanged. The actual original-path/zero-occupancy compression in [F3] gives $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ and $eU^+=U$, with the faithful supporting-block Morita equivalence and natural Hom comparison. Every simple constituent of $V(A^+)$ has the same entry-multiset central character as $A^+$; the bottom-row minimum argument forces every such label to be contractible. Hence the supporting central idempotent satisfies $fV(A^+)=V(A^+)$, and the Hom comparison identifies the original $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))$ with the entire large Hom module, rather than an arbitrary quotient of it. Step 4.1 therefore descends the same intrinsic Specht isomorphism to the original pyramid.

Tilting images and full faithfulness. The opposite-parabolic flag coefficients are the actual tilting-character coefficients of [F1] and [F4]; exact $\pi$ carries each successive standard section to its Specht module by steps 4.1–5.1, so it preserves these flag multiplicities. For fullness, the local corner proof of [F2] applies: in the finite summand algebra $A$, $\pi$ is equivalent to $e(-)$ and has right adjoint $G(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{eAe}(eA,X)$. Its unit on a target with standard socle is injective and has off-standard cokernel. A tilting has standard socle from its standard flag and standard head from its costandard flag and simple-preserving restricted duality. Any map from it to the off-standard cokernel vanishes, since a nonzero quotient would have standard head. Adjunction therefore factors every map between its Schur images uniquely through the original target, proving full faithfulness on tiltings.

Simple images and heads. The finite-W simple-image classification and the genuine Morita equivalence in [F2] and [F3] imply that $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is simple for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, that these are distinct and exhaustive, and that $\pi(L(A))=0$ otherwise. For a standard label $A$, the cover $P(A)$ is an indecomposable summand of $T$, so $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is an indecomposable projective. Its simple quotients are determined by $\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(Y(A),D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P(A),L(B))$, which has dimension $\delta_{A,B}$; this is the ordinary equivalence on $\operatorname{add}(T)$ and the simple-image computation. Thus $Y(A)$ has head $D(A)$. Lift the cover $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$ using projectivity; the lift is surjective since the latter is the simple-head quotient and any proper submodule of $N(A)$ lies in its radical. Exactness yields $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow S(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$. Every nonzero quotient of the indecomposable projective $Y(A)$ has the same simple head $D(A)$: its kernel is contained in the unique maximal submodule. Therefore $S(A)$ has head $D(A)$.

Projective images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, the preceding step shows that $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is the indecomposable projective with simple head $D(A)$, hence its projective cover. Evaluation $T\otimes_{B_d}\pi(P(A))\to P(A)$ is an isomorphism because $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$: this is checked on $T$ and restricted to its idempotent summands. Thus $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$. Off-standard projectives retain their actual images, and no projective-preservation assertion follows for them.

Multiplicities. Since $\pi$ is exact and its kernel is generated by the off-standard simples, the composition multiplicities of $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ are the multiplicities of the simple $L(B)$ in $N(A)$ for $B\in\mathrm{Std}$; by the Fock-space dictionary [F4] the typed coefficient of the dual-canonical/canonical pairing equals $d_{B,A}(1)$, so $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$; for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}$ the module $D(B)$ is zero and is not a simple Hecke label. All the identifications above are ungraded and taken at parameter $1$.
