Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b\le k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b\le k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where $d(s)$ is the permutation determined by $t^\lambda d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+(d-1)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. The cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$.

Let $n\ge1$. (a) The elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ act diagonally in the Young
basis of the previous item: for every standard tableau $T$ of size $n$ and
every $k$, $X_kv_T=c_T(k)v_T$, and the joint eigenspaces are
one-dimensional, indexed by the standard tableaux. (b) A vector
$\alpha=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$ occurs as the joint eigenvalue vector
of a $v_T$, equivalently $\alpha=\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ for a standard
tableau $T$, if and only if: (1) $a_1=0$; (2) for every $q>1$ at least one of
$a_q-1,a_q+1$ occurs among $a_1,\dots,a_{q-1}$; (3) if $a_p=a_q$ with $p<q$,
then both $a_p-1$ and $a_p+1$ occur among $a_{p+1},\dots,a_{q-1}$. The
association $T\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ is a bijection from the standard
tableaux of size $n$ onto this set.

Assume inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the category-O, Fock/global and quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].
For $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ let $D(A)$ be the simple module of the
identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The assignment $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ is an isomorphism from the split
Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ of finite-dimensional
projective modules onto the standard highest weight lattice
$V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$,
so $\{P_A\}$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis; at parameter one the source vector $P_A$
coincides with $T_{A^\uparrow}$, and the lattice is integrally generated by its
ground vector under divided powers.

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
the map $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\to G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ induced

natural injective inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce
operators on $K_0$ that are the Chevalley operators adjoint to their $G_0$
operators of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]].

**(v)** The left adjoint $\pi^*$ of the Schur quotient is right exact on all
modules, sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives and recovers the
standard-labelled prinjectives; exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules is
neither asserted nor needed.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, use the compatible finite cuts and the intrinsic Hecke identity of the $G_0$ theorem. They identify the projective covers and the lower integral basis $P_A$ on every selected content. Consequently (i)–(iv) hold for the full supported tower, including unbounded intervals; clause (v) concerns the Schur functor in each actual stable realization.

Assume the bounded-below setting of the tower: $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is nonempty,
consecutive and bounded below, $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ is an admitted integral
multicharge, and $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], using its actual admissible integral-origin stable realization with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Let
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ be the column-strict, respectively
standard, tableaux of the Fock data of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]], with monomials $M_A$ and
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$, canonical vectors $T_A$ and quasi-canonical vectors
$P_A$ as in [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and
let $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ be the normalized highest projection, so that
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and $S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$. Work at source
parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The exact Schur quotient identifies the module Grothendieck group
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the FULL integral costandard lattice
$$V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\,D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A\ :\ A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\,\}$$
by $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, and it sends every Specht class to
$[S(B)]\mapsto S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$; the vectors
$\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ are another integral basis, the standard
monomial basis.

**(ii)** The endomorphisms of $G_0$ induced by the residue functors $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of the integrable
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock action, and both the standard and the costandard
integral forms carry the actual divided-power action.

**(iii)** Over $\mathbb Q$ the ground class generates the dual highest weight
module $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Over $\mathbb Z$ the costandard lattice need
NOT be ground cyclic, even under divided powers: the rank-one case
$I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ has a ground-generated integral lattice of
index two that omits $D_{01}$. The STANDARD lattice, by contrast, is integrally
generated by its ground vector under divided powers.

**(iv)** Every standard-tableau simple occurs as a composition factor of a
residue word applied to the ground simple, and the ground crystal component is
exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$.

**(v)** The categorical reachability and rational-cyclicity statements of
(iii)-(iv) do not imply integral costandard cyclicity; the level-$0$ tower has
only the ground weight.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, the same statements hold blockwise and sum to the same lattice identifications. Use finite letter cuts containing every charge and finite root cuts containing the selected content and every intermediate content in the chosen residue words. The transition maps append the common ground tail below the lower cut and leave all letters above the upper cut absent. They fix the intrinsic Hecke generators, spectral idempotents and residue bimodules on the selected contents, and identify both integral lattices by their labelled bases. The dual module here is the restricted, weightwise dual, not the unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of

Use the actual source chart at parameter $s$: with the monomials $M_A$ and the
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$ of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], put

$$R_{A,B}(s)=p_{A,B}(-s),\qquad L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A,\qquad M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A . $$

Thus $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ is the INVERSE of $R(s)$, not its transpose. Also
$P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$.

**(i)** For every Specht label $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ and every simple label
$A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $[S(B):D(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$.

**(ii)** In the usual Specht-row/simple-column notation the rectangular
decomposition matrix is the transpose of $D$ restricted to standard rows; it is
NOT the transpose of the $L$-in-$M$ chart. The full matrix $D$ is unitriangular
on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and its square submatrix on standard columns is
unitriangular; in particular $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ only for
$B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, since for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the object
$D(B)=0$ is not a simple module label.

**(iii)** Retain the type-$A$ polynomial formula: for the right place action,
$w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the ENTRY stabilizer $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, and

$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}),$$

while the COLUMN Levi $J$ is a distinct group; the mixed singular/parabolic
composition matrix is the finite Levi cancellation sum over $C$ column-equivalent
to $B$, $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$, and equals
$d_{A,B}(1)$. All categorification multiplicities are ungraded at parameter
one, with the source/library reciprocal convention.

Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible
finite pieces give the original arbitrary-$I$ statement. At level $0$ only
$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.

derivations.claim: **The two charts are mutually inverse.** By [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] the vectors $L_B$ and $M_A$ are two $\mathbb Z[s,s^{-1}]$-bases of the finite weight spaces of the Fock module, so the transition matrices $R(s)=(p_{A,B}(-s))$ with $L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A$ and $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ with $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$ satisfy $R(s)D(s)=D(s)R(s)=1$; both are triangular with diagonal entries $1$ on each weight block, and the quasi-canonical vector is $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$. The polynomial entries and the chart conventions are those of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].

**The type-$A$ polynomial dictionary.** The explicit transition coefficients are given by the type-$A$ formulas of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]: for the right place action, $w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the entry stabilizer $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, $p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2})$, the column Levi $J$ is distinct from $K$, and the mixed singular/parabolic composition coefficient is the finite Levi cancellation sum $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$.

**The O-side multiplicity dictionary.** On the category-O side the standard module $N(B)$ has a composition series whose multiplicities with respect to the simples $L(A)$ are read off in the same chart: the coefficient of $M_B$ in the expansion of $P_A$ is the multiplicity of $L(A)$ in $N(B)$ at parameter one, in the source's reciprocal convention, by [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; combined with step 1.1 this gives $[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for all $A,B$, with $d_{A,B}$ unitriangular, and $[N(B):L(B)]=1$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ in the full square matrix.

**Transfer to the Hecke side.** By [F2] the Schur quotient is exact, sends $N(B)$ to $S(B)$, $L(A)$ to $D(A)$ for standard $A$ and kills the off-standard simples; applying it to a composition series of $N(B)$ and using [F1] gives $[S(B):D(A)]=[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, the sum being finite on each weight block. This proves (i).

**Shape of the matrix.** The full matrix $D=(d_{A,B})$ is unitriangular on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1; restricting rows to the simple labels $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ (all of which occur, and which index the simples by [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]) leaves a rectangular matrix, whose square submatrix on the standard columns is again unitriangular with diagonal entries $1$. The supported weight blocks and labels agree under the actual arbitrary-$I$ cut maps of the $G_0$ theorem, so this same coefficient calculation applies to every admitted consecutive interval. Off standard columns the equation $D(B)=0$ says precisely that $D(B)$ is not a simple module label, so the identity $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ is asserted only for $B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. This proves (ii). The statement is not that the rectangular matrix is invertible, and no off-standard simple is created.

**The polynomial coefficient is not a transposed inverse.** In the coefficient convention used in the proof, the decomposition array has rows the simple labels and columns the Specht labels, and its entries are the coefficients of $D(s)$ at $s=1$; since $R(s)=D(s)^{-1}$, its transpose is $D(s)^{-t}$, which is in general different from the $L$-in-$M$ chart $R(s)$. On the two-factor space with labels $01<10$ one has $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, so $R_{01,10}=-s$ is the negative-entry chart, whereas its inverse has $D_{01,10}=s$, while the true decomposition entry is $d_{01,10}(1)=1$: $S(10)$ is the simple $D(01)$ and not a formal negative combination. Hence with simple rows and Specht columns the decomposition matrix is the standard-row restriction of $D$; with Specht rows and simple columns it is its transpose. Neither convention uses the transpose of $R$. This completes (iii) together with steps 1.2, whose entry stabilizer $K$ and column Levi $J$ remain distinct and whose multiplicities are the finite Levi cancellation values at parameter one; all statements are ungraded.

boundaries.evidence: The ground label B=A_Lambda has the trivial standard composition series, giving the diagonal entry of the standard square submatrix in steps 3.1 and 4.1.
For an off-standard label B the object D(B) is zero and is not a simple label; step 4.1 states the diagonal identity only for standard B.
The two-factor window 01<10 of step 5.1 is the smallest case with a nonzero off-diagonal entry, d_{01,10}(1)=1.

Repeated entries in the multicharge give singular repeated-entry rows; the entry stabilizer K and the column Levi J of step 1.2 are kept distinct exactly so that the mixed singular/parabolic coefficients are read correctly.
The specialization is at the parameter endpoint s=1, where the charts R(s) and D(s) of step 1.1 are evaluated in the source convention.
Step 3.1 applies the exact quotient to a finite composition series; the polynomial dictionary and its supplier assume AC as declared in the Given.

boundaries.reason: The item proves a multiplicity identity and a shape statement rather than a biconditional; the only conditional phrasing, the diagonal one for standard B, is proved directly in step 4.1.
No converse statement is made; in particular the transposed inverse chart is explicitly not identified with the decomposition matrix, as step 5.1 shows.

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the

family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
